title: Aircraft Flow Management under Congestion
finder_method_summary: Earliest stochastic ground-holding model: an idealized star-shaped airway network with congestion only at the central arrival airport and probabilistic landing capacity; chooses ground delays for inbound flights to minimize total expected delay cost and gives a polynomial-time (dynamic-programming style) exact algorithm for this single-period problem.
finder_relevance_note: The star network with one congested node is exactly a RAM regional hub or vertiport fed by many small fields; its polynomial structure suggests fast exact subroutines for per-hub hold assignment inside a larger RAM flow model.

title: Dynamic Ground-Holding Policies for a Network of Airports
finder_method_summary: First dynamic treatment of the multi-airport ground-holding problem: compact pure 0-1 integer programs on a discretized time horizon for a network of airports with connected flights, re-solved as time advances and weather forecasts improve; one formulation lets the arrival/departure capacity mix be updated via runway use.
finder_relevance_note: Provides the rolling-horizon re-solve template a RAM operations centre needs when weather or charger availability updates arrive during the day.

title: The Multi-Airport Ground-Holding Problem in Air Traffic Control
finder_method_summary: First network (multi-airport) ground-holding formulation: several 0-1 integer programs assign ground holds to flights over discrete time periods subject to per-period arrival/departure capacities at each airport, with flights coupled through aircraft continuation (down-the-road delay propagation). Solved by LP relaxation plus a rounding heuristic; instances with 6 airports and 3,000 flights solved in reasonable time.
finder_relevance_note: Aircraft-connectivity constraints are exactly what links successive RAM legs of a small electric fleet through turnaround and charging; this is the first network-level GHP that models them.

title: Optimal Algorithms and a Remarkably Efficient Heuristic for the Ground-Holding Problem in Air Traffic Control
finder_method_summary: Compares optimal static and dynamic stochastic-LP solutions to the single-airport ground-holding problem with a very fast heuristic that uses probabilistic landing-capacity forecasts and accounts for the dynamic nature of decisions; on Boston Logan data the heuristic beats the static optimum and deterministic approaches and is within 5% of the dynamic optimum at a fraction of the computing time.
finder_relevance_note: Shows when a cheap slot-assignment heuristic suffices at a single capacity-constrained regional airport, useful as the inner solver in a decomposed RAM network model.

title: The Air Traffic Flow Management Problem with Enroute Capacities
finder_method_summary: The canonical BSP model: a time-indexed 0-1 IP with cumulative variables (flight f has reached sector j by time t) that enforces airport arrival/departure and en-route sector capacities per period, with ground holding, airborne holding and speed control chosen jointly. Shows the formulation is strong (several inequalities are facet-defining, LP bound at least as tight as earlier models), extends to rerouting and hub-and-spoke banks, and solves instances with thousands of flights.
finder_relevance_note: The by-time variable discretization is the standard way to encode departure-time assignment and holds on a time-expanded network; for RAM it extends directly to vertiport/regional-airport, airspace and charging-slot capacities per period.

title: The Traffic Flow Management Rerouting Problem in Air Traffic Control: A Dynamic Network Flow Approach
finder_method_summary: Formulates ATFM with ground holding, airborne holding and rerouting as an integer dynamic multicommodity network flow problem with side constraints on a time-expanded airspace network (airports and sectors as nodes, time-indexed arcs, per-period airport and sector capacities). Solved by a Lagrangian relaxation scheme (Lagrangian generation) that aggregates flights into commodity flows, solves the relaxed network problem, and disaggregates back to integral flight routes and schedules via randomized rounding; near-optimal solutions reported on national-scale instances.
finder_relevance_note: The RAM flow problem is exactly a dynamic multicommodity flow on a time-expanded regional network with airport/airspace capacities, and the aggregate-then-disaggregate Lagrangian scheme suits many small-aircraft flights; the same machinery gives the operational flow sub-problem of a spaceport feeder network.

title: The European Air Traffic Flow Management Problem
finder_method_summary: Integer program on a time-expanded network with binding en-route sector capacities (European setting) that assigns ground and airborne holds; shows that minimising total delay can produce inequitable, non-FCFS allocations and introduces equity-related objective terms to study the efficiency-equity trade-off.
finder_relevance_note: RAM corridors between small airports resemble the en-route-constrained European case more than the airport-constrained US case, so the model's treatment of airborne holding and the equity side effects transfer directly.

title: A dynamic rerouting model for air traffic flow management
finder_method_summary: Stochastic integer programming model for traffic inbound to one airport when both the airport and its approach routes/arrival fixes are subject to adverse weather; jointly decides ground holding and dynamic rerouting among arrival routes over a capacity scenario tree; dynamic rerouting cuts delay cost 10-15% versus static rerouting and about 50% versus pure ground holding.
finder_relevance_note: Gives the dynamic (multi-stage) version of the time-expanded flow model, directly applicable to RAM flows whose airspace or weather capacity is revealed over the day.

title: An Integer Optimization Approach to Large-Scale Air Traffic Flow Management
finder_method_summary: Integer optimization model jointly deciding ground holding, airborne holding, rerouting and speed control for every flight, using cumulative time-indexed variables on a sector graph with route choice encoded via sector-adjacency (local routing) constraints. Facet-defining inequalities are identified and the LP relaxation is shown to be integral in most cases; instances with about 6,500 flights and 145 sectors (US-NAS scale) are solved in minutes.
finder_relevance_note: Shows that a single time-indexed flow formulation can absorb routing and speed decisions for very many flights, which is the scale regime of a RAM network with many small electric aircraft.

title: On the Impact of Scheduling Limits: A Case Study at Newark Liberty International Airport
finder_method_summary: Evaluates airport scheduling limits (slot caps) by combining an IP that smooths/displaces the schedule to meet a cap with a stochastic queuing delay model, quantifying the delay response to alternative caps at Newark.
finder_relevance_note: The schedule-displacement IP is the strategic demand-management counterpart for RAM airports whose hourly caps are set by pads, chargers or noise rules.

id: title:dynamic airspace sectorisation for flight centric operations
title: Dynamic airspace sectorisation for flight-centric operations
finder_method_summary: Dynamic sectorisation that shifts from 'flow follows structure' to 'structure follows flow': sectors are built around actual traffic flows (flight-centric operations) to balance controller workload under operational, economic and ecological constraints.
finder_relevance_note: Flow-driven capacity partitioning is relevant to defining time-varying airspace capacity constraints for RAM networks.

title: Central Authority-Controlled Air Traffic Flow Management: An Optimization Approach
authors: Hamdan, Cheaitou, Jouini, Andersson Granberg, Jemai, Alsyouf, Bettayeb, Josefsson
finder_method_summary: Integer programming ATFM model with path rerouting and diversion options plus pre-existing en-route flights, comparing a central-authority regime (controls all ground/air delay, reroute, cancellation decisions) with decentralised ATFM-authority/airline decisions; includes inter-flight and inter-airline fairness measures; exact solution for small/medium instances and a modified fix-and-relax heuristic for large ones. Reported delay reductions up to 8% and cancellations up to 23%; fairness costs 0.2-3.0%.
finder_relevance_note: A recent centralized flow-control model that a single RAM network operator could adopt directly for departure-time, route and hold assignment.

title: Predictive and Prescriptive Analytics Toward Passenger-Centric Ground Delay Programs
finder_method_summary: Large-scale integer optimisation for GDPs that balances flight and passenger delays (including misconnections), combined with statistical learning models that predict passenger itineraries; shows passenger delays fall substantially for small flight-delay cost increases via delay allocation and deliberate delay introduction, and that results are robust to itinerary misprediction.
finder_relevance_note: RAM itineraries will often be multi-leg feeder trips; predicting itineraries and allocating holds to protect connections is directly transferable.

title: Data-Driven Optimization for Air Traffic Flow Management with Trajectory Preferences
finder_method_summary: Trajectory-based ATFM in which airspace users' trajectory preferences are learned from historical traffic by clustering and classification, then a binary integer program assigns each flight a feasible 4D trajectory and possible ground delay subject to sector and airport capacities; Eurocontrol instances with more than 32,000 flights solve in practical times.
finder_relevance_note: Shows how to learn operator preferences from data and still solve a network-scale IP, relevant for on-demand RAM where operator utilities are heterogeneous.

title: A Stochastic Integer Program with Dual Network Structure and Its Application to the Ground-Holding Problem
authors: Ball, Hoffman, Odoni, Rifkin (title/authors matched to IDEAS OR 51(1):167-171 record)
finder_method_summary: Static stochastic ground-holding model with aggregate per-period demand and a scenario set for airport arrival capacity; proves the constraint matrix is dual network (totally unimodular) so the stochastic IP can be solved as an LP / network flow; output is a planned arrival-rate profile that plugs into CDM ground delay program procedures (slot allocation).
finder_relevance_note: A reusable structural result: RAM slot planning at a weather-limited regional airport can be formulated to inherit this integrality and solve as an LP inside a larger decomposition.

title: A Dynamic Stochastic Model for the Single Airport Ground Holding Problem
finder_method_summary: Multistage dynamic stochastic integer program for the single-airport GHP in which airport capacity evolves along a scenario tree and ground delays assigned to individual flights can be revised at each decision stage as weather forecasts update; LP relaxation observed to yield integer solutions; includes intra-airline substitution/cancellation to fit CDM; gains largest under stringent ground-holding policy, early GDP cancellation and low bad/good-weather capacity ratios; optimal policy releases long-haul flights on time and uses short-haul flights to absorb delay.
finder_relevance_note: RAM flights are short-haul and highly revisable, exactly the flights this model uses as the flexible recourse; the scenario-tree multistage structure transfers to RAM departure-time revision under evolving airport/vertiport capacity.

title: Scenario-based air traffic flow management: From theory to practice
finder_method_summary: Methodology for building the capacity scenarios and scenario trees that static and dynamic stochastic ground-holding models require: clusters empirical airport capacity profiles into a small number of nominal scenarios and identifies branch points where profiles diverge; finds most US airports have few nominal profiles that combine naturally into trees; demonstrates use in stochastic GHP models.
finder_relevance_note: Provides the recipe for turning historical capacity data into tractable scenario trees, needed for RAM airports with sparse history and for spaceport launch-window availability profiles alike.

title: Airport congestion management under uncertainty
finder_method_summary: Analytical comparison of congestion pricing and slot (quantity) instruments for airport congestion management under uncertainty.
finder_relevance_note: Price-versus-quantity analysis under demand/capacity uncertainty informs how to ration RAM airport capacity or launch windows when demand is uncertain.

title: Determining Stochastic Airspace Capacity for Air Traffic Flow Management
finder_method_summary: Fast simulation-based method for the stochastic capacity of an airspace region: ensemble weather forecasts are combined with an air-traffic-control routing algorithm in an integrated weather-traffic model to produce time-varying probabilistic capacity maps for use as inputs to stochastic ATFM models, addressing capacity left unused by deterministic decisions.
finder_relevance_note: Provides the airspace-side counterpart to airport capacity scenarios, needed for RAM low-altitude corridors and for the airspace closures a spaceport launch imposes on surrounding traffic.

title: Incorporating Predictability Into Cost Optimization for Ground Delay Programs
finder_method_summary: Introduces predictability (dispersion of realized delay) into GDP cost optimization under capacity uncertainty and develops two stochastic GDP models, a static no-revision model and a dynamic model allowing one GDP revision, to trade expected delay cost against unpredictability.
finder_relevance_note: RAM passengers and charging logistics value predictable departure times; this gives a way to price unpredictability inside a stochastic hold model.

title: Air traffic flow management under uncertainty using chance-constrained optimization
finder_method_summary: Chance-constrained formulation of the ATFM problem (ground/airborne holding on a time-expanded flight network) in which sector/airport capacity constraints must hold with prescribed probability under weather-driven capacity uncertainty; reformulated to a tractable deterministic (mixed-integer) equivalent and tested on US airspace instances. TR-B 102:124-141.
finder_relevance_note: Chance-constrained capacity handling transfers to RAM airport/charging slots and to launch-window capacity under weather uncertainty in spaceport feeder networks.

title: Dynamic Control of Runway Configurations and of Arrival and Departure Service Rates at JFK Airport Under Stochastic Queue Conditions
finder_method_summary: Dynamic programming model that jointly and dynamically selects runway configuration and the arrival/departure service-rate split to minimize congestion cost under stochastic queue dynamics and stochastic weather/wind; state includes schedules, queue lengths and weather; exact DP solves in reasonable time at JFK and a one-step look-ahead approximation gives near-optimal policies much faster.
finder_relevance_note: Endogenous capacity control via DP is relevant to RAM airports/vertiports where the manager can reconfigure pads, runways or charging stalls in response to queues and weather.

title: Stochastic Runway Scheduling
finder_method_summary: Stochastic runway sequencing and scheduling with uncertain aircraft ready times formulated as a two-stage stochastic integer program and solved with sample-based decomposition/branching techniques, extending the authors' stochastic branch-and-bound work to a rigorous stochastic programming treatment.
finder_relevance_note: Stochastic sequence-then-time structure transfers to RAM departure/arrival slotting with uncertain turnaround and charging completion times, and to launch-slot scheduling under weather/readiness uncertainty.

title: A Stochastic Integer Programming Approach to Air Traffic Scheduling and Operations
finder_method_summary: Integrated model of strategic scheduling interventions and tactical ground-holding across an airport network under operating uncertainty, formulated as a two-stage stochastic program with integer recourse; an original decomposition algorithm with provable solution-quality guarantees uses new dual integer cuts derived from reduced costs of the second-stage LP dual.
finder_relevance_note: Joint strategic scheduling + tactical holding under uncertainty is the template for RAM timetable design and for feeder launch schedule design with recourse.

title: Air Traffic Control Capacity Planning Under Demand and Capacity Provision Uncertainty
authors: Starita, Strauss, Fei, Jovanović, Ivanov, Pavlović, Fichert
finder_method_summary: Stochastic optimization of future ATC capacity provision (controller sector-hours and sector opening schemes) against uncertain traffic and uncertain delivered capacity; a scalable decomposition approach exploits problem structure to handle a large number of traffic scenarios; several decision policies are tested on real European data.
finder_relevance_note: Capacity-provision planning under demand uncertainty is the strategic question for sizing RAM airspace services and for spaceport/range capacity ahead of uncertain launch demand.

id: title:two stage stochastic mixed integer programming with chance constraints for extended aircra
title: Two-Stage Stochastic Mixed-Integer Programming with Chance Constraints for Extended Aircraft Arrival Management
finder_method_summary: Extended arrival management as a two-stage stochastic MIP with chance constraints: first stage fixes the sequence and target times over the initial approach fix to minimize landing-sequence length; actual times deviate randomly, and the second stage sets landing times minimizing time-deviation costs while separation constraints hold with high probability; solved via scenario-based approximation.
finder_relevance_note: Combines sequencing, target-time setting and probabilistic separation, the structure needed for metering RAM arrivals into a regional airport with uncertain flight times.

id: title:cross border capacity planning in air traffic management under uncertainty
title: Cross-Border Capacity Planning in Air Traffic Management Under Uncertainty
authors: Starita, Strauss, Fei, Jovanović, Ivanov, Pavlović, Fichert
finder_method_summary: Extends the 2020 stochastic ATC capacity-planning model to coordinated cross-border capacity provision among several air navigation service providers under traffic and capacity uncertainty, using scenario-based stochastic optimization with decomposition to compare coordinated and uncoordinated policies.
finder_relevance_note: Multi-jurisdiction capacity coordination under uncertainty parallels RAM networks spanning several regional airport owners and spaceport-range coordination with adjacent airspace.

title: An Airspace Planning Model for Selecting Flight-plans Under Workload, Safety, and Equity Considerations
finder_method_summary: 0-1 integer program selecting one flight plan per flight from alternatives to minimise fuel/delay cost subject to sector workload, conflict/safety and inter-airline equity constraints (bounds on each airline's relative cost deviation); motivated by special-use-airspace closures for space launches; solved by branch-and-bound with valid inequalities.
finder_relevance_note: The one-plan-per-flight assignment IP with strengthening transfers to RAM corridor/time selection, and the model explicitly handles airspace closures around spaceport launches, linking topics A and B.

title: An Airspace Planning and Collaborative Decision-Making Model: Part I—Probabilistic Conflicts, Workload, and Equity Considerations
finder_method_summary: Extends the airspace planning model into a collaborative decision-making framework: a mixed-integer program selects flight plans from airline-submitted alternatives subject to probabilistic conflict (safety) constraints, sector workload limits and inter-airline equity measures.
finder_relevance_note: Supplies the probabilistic-conflict and equity constraint structure for a collaborative RAM flow model where several small operators submit preferred trajectories.

title: An Airspace-Planning and Collaborative Decision-Making Model: Part II—Cost Model, Data Considerations, and Computations
finder_method_summary: Develops the fuel/delay cost model and data treatment for the APCDM 0-1 integer program and reports computational results on realistic instances with equity (cost-sharing) considerations.
finder_relevance_note: Shows how to make the flight-plan selection IP solve at realistic scale, the computational side a RAM implementation would need.

title: Equitable Models for the Stochastic Ground-Holding Problem Under Collaborative Decision Making
finder_method_summary: Static stochastic integer programs for the single-airport ground-holding problem under capacity scenarios, modified so that slot assignments respect CDM equity (airline-ordered flight sets / RBS-consistent allocations); analyses the polyhedral structure and the cost of imposing equity.
finder_relevance_note: RAM will involve several operators sharing scarce regional-airport and charging capacity; equity-constrained stochastic rationing is the template for a fair RAM demand-capacity balancing service.

title: Slot Trading Opportunities in Collaborative Ground Delay Programs
finder_method_summary: Models CDM slot exchange after a ration-by-schedule (RBS) initial allocation of arrival slots at one airport: inter-airline slot trades (a generalisation of the compression algorithm) are formulated as assignment / network-flow integer programs over a flight-to-slot bipartite structure with airline-declared substitutions, including a mediated-bartering variant; shows delay-cost gains over compression.
finder_relevance_note: Gives the single-resource slot-assignment and mediated-exchange machinery a RAM scheduler needs to let scheduled and on-demand operators swap departure, arrival or charger slots at a capacity-constrained regional airport after a proportional initial allocation.

id: title:reallocating arrival slots during a ground delay program
title: Reallocating arrival slots during a ground delay program
finder_method_summary: Airline-side arrival-slot reallocation problem in response to a GDP, minimising flight delay and passenger missed-connection costs; formulated as a dynamic program solved by branch and bound within a rolling-horizon framework; practical instances solved within five minutes.
finder_relevance_note: Operator-side substitution/reallocation model that complements the mediator-side CDM models for RAM operators holding multiple slots.

title: Analysis of performance and equity in ground delay programs
finder_method_summary: Analysis of GDP performance and equity metrics (flight- and passenger-based) across GDP rationing/exemption configurations.
finder_relevance_note: Supplies equity metrics for evaluating RAM flow-management outcomes across operators and passengers.

id: title:congestion pricing slot sales and slot trading in aviation
title: Congestion pricing, slot sales and slot trading in aviation
finder_method_summary: Analytical duopoly model of airlines at a congested airport addressing uninternalized congestion and market power. Derives first-best (airline-differentiated) charges, shows undifferentiated charges are a weighted average and less efficient, and shows tradable slots reach first-best only when congestion dominates the market-power distortion.
finder_relevance_note: Economic foundations for slot/charging mechanisms that allocate scarce airport capacity among regional operators.

title: Ground Delay Program Planning Under Uncertainty Based on the Ration-by-Distance Principle
finder_method_summary: GDP planning under airport-capacity uncertainty using ration-by-distance (RBD): ground delay is assigned preferentially to short-haul flights that can still exploit late capacity information, with explicit equity guarantees expressed as bounded deviation from the RBS allocation; stochastic analysis shows RBD approaches the minimum expected delay while keeping airline equity.
finder_relevance_note: Shows how distance (flight time) to the constrained resource should drive who is held under cancellation uncertainty; RAM has very heterogeneous short stage lengths, making the RBD logic directly applicable.

id: title:pricing vs slot policies when airport profits matter
title: Pricing vs. slot policies when airport profits matter
finder_relevance_note: Benchmark for price versus quantity instruments when scarce take-off/landing or launch-window capacity is allocated by a profit-seeking infrastructure owner.

title: Integrating Slot Exchange, Safety, Capacity, and Equity Mechanisms Within an Airspace Flow Program
finder_relevance_note: Combines rerouting under airspace constraints with slot trading and equity, the situation RAM faces during weather or launch-related airspace closures.

title: The Price of Fairness
finder_method_summary: Introduces the price of fairness, the relative efficiency loss of a fair allocation, and derives bounds for proportional fairness and max-min fairness in resource allocation problems.
finder_relevance_note: Gives the theoretical bound on efficiency lost when slots or launch capacity are allocated fairly among operators.

title: Equitable and Efficient Coordination in Traffic Flow Management
finder_method_summary: Augments the Bertsimas-Stock Patterson 0-1 IP on a time-expanded network with sector and airport capacities with a network fairness metric that generalises RBS (time-order deviation, reversals and overtaking), penalised in the objective; national-scale instances show large equity gains for small efficiency loss.
finder_relevance_note: The reversal/overtaking fairness constraints can be added verbatim to a time-expanded RAM flow IP in which several operators compete for corridor and airport capacity.

title: Ground delay program planning: Delay, equity, and computational complexity
finder_method_summary: Analyses GDP planning as a slot-assignment problem with delay and equity (RBS-based) objectives, gives computational-complexity results and integer-programming / heuristic approaches.
finder_relevance_note: Clarifies which equity-constrained slot-assignment variants are tractable before embedding them in a RAM flow model.

id: title:stochastic optimization models for ground delay program planning with equity efficiency tr
title: Stochastic optimization models for ground delay program planning with equity-efficiency tradeoffs
finder_method_summary: Two-stage stochastic integer programs for GDP planning (program scope and rates) over capacity scenarios, with a multiobjective treatment of total expected delay versus an equity measure based on deviation from RBS.
finder_relevance_note: The two-stage stochastic multi-objective structure is a direct template for RAM demand-capacity balancing where operators with different stage lengths must be treated fairly.

title: The time slot allocation problem under uncertain capacity
finder_method_summary: Two two-stage stochastic programming models for strategic allocation of airport time slots across a network of airports with uncertain capacity; first stage allocates slots respecting airline requests and operational constraints, second stage captures operational delays under capacity scenarios; exposes the tradeoff between schedule displacement from requests and expected operational delay.
finder_relevance_note: Directly transferable to seasonal slot coordination at capacity-constrained regional airports under weather uncertainty, and analogous to allocating launch windows at a spaceport whose usable capacity is uncertain.

title: Fairness and Collaboration in Network Air Traffic Flow Management: An Optimization Approach
finder_method_summary: Two-stage approach: a network ATFM integer program on a time-expanded network with fairness controls (reversals/overtaking), followed by an airline-collaboration stage in which each airline re-optimises flight-to-slot substitutions within its own allocation via network-flow / IP models; large US instances show a tractable efficiency-fairness-collaboration trade-off.
finder_relevance_note: Demonstrates that the cumulative-variable network model keeps scaling when fairness side constraints are added, which a multi-operator RAM network would need.

title: An optimization approach for airport slot allocation under IATA guidelines
finder_method_summary: Priority-based Slot Allocation Model: a lexicographic multi-objective integer program implementing IATA priority classes (historic, change-to-historic, new entrants), schedule-displacement objectives and series-of-slots regularity constraints under rolling-window capacity limits, solved sequentially and applied to Portuguese airports.
finder_relevance_note: The lexicographic priority structure is the natural way to encode operator classes (scheduled vs on-demand, incumbent vs new entrant) in RAM slot coordination and in launch-window allocation.

title: Incorporating Stakeholders' priorities and preferences in 4D trajectory optimization
authors: Dal Sasso, Djeumou Fomeni, Lulli, Zografos
finder_method_summary: Integer programming model that selects one 4D trajectory per flight from airspace-user-submitted alternatives (route/level/time options) subject to sector and airport capacity on a time-discretised network, while incorporating stakeholders' priorities and preferences through a multi-criteria objective; TR-B 117(Part A):594-609.
finder_relevance_note: Trajectory-option selection with operator priorities is the trajectory-based-operations form of the RAM flow problem (choice among a few corridor/altitude/time options per flight).

title: Interairline Equity in Airport Scheduling Interventions
finder_method_summary: Integrated Capacity Utilization and Scheduling Model with Equity Considerations: schedule-displacement optimisation coupled with a stochastic queuing model of capacity utilisation, with explicit inter-airline equity objectives; on JFK scenarios the model prioritises airlines equally with little or no efficiency loss.
finder_relevance_note: Shows how to add operator-equity objectives to strategic schedule-coordination models that would cap demand at congested RAM airports or vertiports.

title: A Large-Scale Neighborhood Search Approach to Airport Slot Allocation
finder_method_summary: Large-scale neighbourhood search for slot allocation at large coordinated airports: a constructive heuristic builds a feasible schedule and an improvement heuristic iteratively re-optimises subsets of slot requests with the IP model; at Lisbon it finds optimal or near-optimal solutions in hours where commercial solvers do not terminate after days.
finder_relevance_note: Decomposition-by-request-subset heuristics apply to any large slot-assignment IP, including seasonal RAM schedule coordination.

title: A Slot-Scheduling Mechanism at Congested Airports that Incorporates Efficiency, Fairness, and Airline Preferences
finder_method_summary: Two-stage slot-scheduling mechanism: stage 1 constructs a reference schedule that is fair to airlines (efficiency and fairness objectives); stage 2 lets each airline specify how its total displacement should be distributed among its requests, and the mechanism adjusts the schedule to satisfy as many preferences as possible; IP models throughout.
finder_relevance_note: A preference-elicitation layer on top of a fair reference allocation is directly reusable for allocating slots among competing RAM operators.

id: title:a framework for collaborative air traffic flow management minimizing costs for airspace us
title: A framework for collaborative air traffic flow management minimizing costs for airspace users: Enabling trajectory options and flexible pre-tactical delay management
finder_method_summary: Collaborative ATFM framework in which airspace users submit trajectory options (alternative routes/levels, linear holding, in-flight delay recovery) and a network-level optimisation assigns options and pre-tactical delays to resolve demand-capacity hotspots at minimum user cost; integer programming on sector-capacity hotspots; TR-B 134:229-255.
finder_relevance_note: Cost-based option selection with flexible delay absorption (ground vs. airborne vs. speed) is directly applicable to RAM flow management where electric aircraft have asymmetric costs of ground vs. in-flight delay.

title: Equity and Strength in Stochastic Integer Programming Models for the Dynamic Single Airport Ground-Holding Problem
finder_method_summary: Dynamic (multistage) stochastic integer programming formulations of the single-airport ground-holding problem; studies the equity properties of their solutions relative to RBS-type allocations and the strength (LP relaxation / integrality) of alternative formulations.
finder_relevance_note: Recent evidence on which equity-constrained slot formulations stay tight, relevant when fairness across RAM operators is embedded in a decomposed network model.

title: Synchronised demand-capacity balancing in collaborative air traffic flow management
finder_method_summary: Mixed-integer model that jointly assigns each flight a delay and a choice among alternative trajectories and, for each airspace block and time period, a sector opening scheme (or dynamic sectorisation); per-period sector capacities couple the two. Solved as an integrated MIP with pre-generated trajectory and sectorisation options; shows large delay reductions versus sequential practice.
finder_relevance_note: Makes the capacity profile itself a decision (time-varying airspace configuration), the airspace analogue of time-varying link capacity in DTA; for RAM, low-altitude corridor structure can likewise be reconfigured over the day alongside flow regulation.

title: Optimal network-wide adjustments of initial airport slot allocations with connectivity and fairness objectives
finder_method_summary: Network-level model that adjusts single-airport initial slot allocations so that aircraft rotations remain connectable across airports, optimising connectivity together with fairness among airlines in a multi-objective integer program.
finder_relevance_note: Network-wide slot coordination with fairness is directly the strategic layer of a multi-airport RAM schedule where aircraft rotations couple slots at different airports.

title: Passenger-Centric Slot Allocation at Schedule-Coordinated Airports
finder_relevance_note: Passenger-weighted slot allocation is relevant when RAM demand is on-demand and passenger itineraries drive priorities.

title: A User-Driven Prioritisation Process implementation and optimisation for ATFM hotspot resolution
finder_method_summary: Studies UDPP solutions letting airlines prioritise their own flights within ATFM regulations; shows that with an accurate delay cost model the prioritisation can be fully automated via an integer programming model, and uses it for cost-benefit estimates of UDPP against the current ATFM regulation process.
finder_relevance_note: Operator-side re-prioritisation within assigned slots is reusable for RAM operators managing their own fleet rotations under flow constraints.

title: Multiairport Ground Holding Problem: A Computational Evaluation of Exact Algorithms
finder_method_summary: Computational comparison of exact algorithms for the multiairport ground holding problem (own algorithms vs Vranas-Bertsimas-Odoni and Bertsimas-Stock formulations) when arrival capacity is limited at congested airports.
finder_relevance_note: Benchmarks formulation strength and exact-method scalability for networked holding problems.

title: Selected Topics in Column Generation
finder_method_summary: Survey of column generation / Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition theory and practice: pricing, dual stabilization, branch-and-price, acceleration strategies; standard methodological reference.
finder_relevance_note: Methodological backbone for path/trajectory-based ATFM and for service-network-design formulations of feeder networks.

id: title:a dual decomposition method for sector capacity constrained traffic flow optimization
title: A dual decomposition method for sector capacity constrained traffic flow optimization
finder_method_summary: Aggregate (Eulerian) multicommodity network model of NAS traffic; minimizing total travel time under sector capacity constraints is posed as a large IP/LP. Dual decomposition on the capacity constraints splits the problem into independent per-commodity subproblems solvable in parallel, making NAS-scale LPs tractable.
finder_relevance_note: Aggregate-flow dual decomposition is a scalable alternative to flight-level IPs for RAM corridor flows and for capacity-coupled time-expanded feeder networks.

title: The Benders Dual Decomposition Method
finder_method_summary: Combines Benders decomposition with Lagrangian dual decomposition for two-stage stochastic integer programs with integer recourse, producing stronger optimality cuts than classical Benders; tested on stochastic network design and facility location instances.
finder_relevance_note: Integer recourse (discrete launch assignments per scenario) is where classical Benders for hub design weakens; this method is the remedy for stochastic spaceport-to-hub models.

title: Partial Benders Decomposition: General Methodology and Application to Stochastic Network Design
finder_method_summary: Strengthens Benders decomposition for two-stage stochastic programs by retaining explicit scenario-subproblem information (retained or artificial scenarios) in the master problem; applied to two-stage stochastic multicommodity network design with stochastic demands and arc capacities, improving efficiency, solution quality and stability. Published online December 2020, print volume 55(2) 2021.
finder_relevance_note: Exact decomposition for scenario-based launch network design with both uncertain demand and uncertain launch-window capacity; the same machinery scales stochastic flow-management models.

id: title:the value of flexible flight to route assignments in pre tactical air traffic management
title: The value of flexible flight-to-route assignments in pre-tactical air traffic management
authors: Starita, Strauss, Fei, Jovanović, Ivanov, Pavlović, Fichert
finder_relevance_note: Deferring route commitment is a natural strategy for RAM operations with uncertain weather and charging availability.

id: title:a mathematical model for predicting the number of potential conflict situations at interse
title: A Mathematical Model for Predicting the Number of Potential Conflict Situations at Intersecting Air Routes
finder_method_summary: Probabilistic model of the expected number of potential conflicts at the intersection of air routes as a function of flows, speeds and crossing angle. TS 7(2):158-167.
finder_relevance_note: Earliest analytical conflict-rate model; basis for complexity/capacity estimates of route crossings in regional route networks.

id: title:a mathematical model for predicting the duration of potential conflict situations at inter
title: A Mathematical Model for Predicting the Duration of Potential Conflict Situations at Intersecting Air Routes
finder_method_summary: Companion probabilistic model giving the expected duration of potential conflicts at intersecting air routes. TS 8(1):58-64.
finder_relevance_note: Conflict-duration estimates feed controller-workload and capacity models for crossing regional routes.

title: En Route Sector Capacity Model
finder_method_summary: Analytical model of en-route sector capacity from the geometry of routes and the concept of expected capacity under saturation (controller continuously busy), relating traffic mix, route configuration and separation to sector throughput. TS 25(4):299-307.
finder_relevance_note: Classic analytical basis for the sector-capacity parameters used as constraints in flow models; adaptable to regional sectors.

title: A simulation based study of subliminal control for air traffic management
finder_method_summary: Simulation study of subliminal (small speed-change) control in en-route ATM, precursor to the Rey et al. optimization models. year inferred from DOI (2010 online).
finder_relevance_note: Evidence base for how much delay/conflict reduction small speed adjustments can deliver before resorting to holds.

id: title:a multi objective approach for dynamic airspace sectorization using agent based and geomet
title: A multi-objective approach for Dynamic Airspace Sectorization using agent based and geometric models
finder_method_summary: Multi-objective genetic algorithm sectorises airspace balancing controller workload, maximizing average sector flight time and maximizing distance between sector boundaries and flow crossing points, using an agent-based traffic model and geometric (region-growing) sector construction.
finder_relevance_note: Multi-objective sector design offers a way to define capacity regions for RAM-scale airspace with heterogeneous traffic.

title: Identification of Robust Terminal-Area Routes in Convective Weather
finder_method_summary: Translates convective-weather forecasts into probabilistic route-blockage forecasts via machine learning (classifying whether a route will be open), then optimizes terminal-area operations by dynamically relocating arrival/departure routes to maximize expected capacity. TS 46(1):56-73.
finder_relevance_note: Data-driven route-availability forecasting feeds stochastic capacity parameters for RAM terminal-area and low-altitude routes.

id: title:some insights into a sequential resource allocation mechanism for en route air traffic man
title: Some insights into a sequential resource allocation mechanism for en route air traffic management
finder_method_summary: Game-theoretic model of sequential capacity allocation in a congestible system: analyses the First-Submitted-First-Assigned (FSFA) process of an en-route flow program such as CTOP, deriving airline submission incentives and allocation outcomes. TR-B 79:1-15.
finder_relevance_note: Incentive analysis for sequential slot/route allocation applies to many small RAM operators competing for constrained airspace or vertiport capacity.

title: Exact and Approximate Solving of the Aircraft Collision Resolution Problem via Turn Changes
finder_method_summary: Mixed 0-1 nonlinear model for conflict detection and resolution using heading (turn) changes under the geometric separation condition; solved exactly with a global MINLP solver and approximately with a sequential/heuristic scheme. TS 50(1):263-274.
finder_relevance_note: Heading-change deconfliction model transferable to en-route separation assurance in free-route regional airspace with many small aircraft.

title: Subliminal Speed Control in Air Traffic Management: Optimization and Simulation
finder_method_summary: Deterministic conflict-resolution models restricted to minor (subliminal) speed adjustments, formulated as nonlinear optimization problems minimizing controller-workload indicators over a potential-conflict set; validated by simulation under perturbations, showing a large share of potential conflicts can be removed with a narrow speed-modulation range and little delay. TS 50(1):240-262.
finder_relevance_note: Speed-modulation-only deconfliction is the natural tactical complement to departure-time/ground-hold assignment in a RAM flow model.

id: title:flight and passenger delay assignment optimization strategies
title: Flight and passenger delay assignment optimization strategies
finder_method_summary: Optimization strategies for assigning ATFM delay to flights considering flight-centric versus passenger-centric objectives. From title/URL only.
finder_relevance_note: Passenger-centric delay allocation objectives matter for RAM where small aircraft make per-passenger impacts visible.

id: title:maximizing airborne delay at no extra fuel cost by means of linear holding
title: Maximizing airborne delay at no extra fuel cost by means of linear holding
finder_method_summary: Linear-holding (speed reduction at no extra fuel) strategy extended from cruise to climb and descent using aircraft-performance data; evaluates keeping vs. changing the requested cruise flight level to maximize holding time, with airborne delay roughly 2-3x earlier estimates for short/mid-haul flights. TR-C 81:137-152.
finder_relevance_note: Quantifies the airborne-delay capacity usable as a decision variable in RAM demand-capacity balancing for short-haul flights.

title: Solving the Air Conflict Resolution Problem Under Uncertainty Using an Iterative Biobjective Mixed Integer Programming Approach
finder_method_summary: Tactical conflict resolution under wind, speed-prediction and maneuver-execution uncertainty. A geometric derivation gives the minimum inter-aircraft distance and conflict probability, which are embedded in a deterministic maximum-clique-of-minimum-weight model on a graph whose vertices are candidate maneuvers; an iterative biobjective MIP trades maneuver cost against conflict probability. TS 51(4):1242-1258.
finder_relevance_note: Maneuver-graph MIP with probabilistic separation is directly reusable for strategic/tactical deconfliction of dense small-aircraft RAM traffic where trajectory prediction is noisy.

id: title:three dimensional conflict count models for unstructured and layered airspace designs
title: Three-dimensional conflict count models for unstructured and layered airspace designs
finder_method_summary: Analytical models of instantaneous conflict counts as a function of traffic demand and airspace design parameters (separation requirements, heading range per flight level) for unstructured and layered en-route airspace, including climbing/descending traffic; validated by fast-time simulation, which showed climbing/descending traffic causes most conflicts in narrow-heading-range layered designs.
finder_relevance_note: Gives an analytic airspace-capacity function (conflicts vs. density and structure) that can serve as the sector/airspace capacity constraint in a UAM or RAM demand-capacity balancing model.

title: A Simulated Annealing Approach to 3D Strategic Aircraft Deconfliction based on En-Route Speed Changes under Wind and Temperature Uncertainties
finder_method_summary: Strategic (pre-departure) 3D deconfliction of 4D trajectories using en-route speed changes, with wind and temperature uncertainty handled via ensemble forecasts; solved by simulated annealing. TR-C 103:194-210. DOI quoted in a citing paper's reference list.
finder_relevance_note: Metaheuristic strategic deconfliction under weather uncertainty scales to network-wide RAM trajectory planning.

id: title:from free route air traffic to an adapted dynamic main flow system
title: From free-route air traffic to an adapted dynamic main-flow system
finder_method_summary: Derives a dynamic main-flow (corridor-like) structure from free-route traffic to organise en-route flows adaptively. From title/URL only; year inferred from PII.
finder_relevance_note: Bridges free-route operations and structured flows, relevant to deciding whether RAM airspace should be structured or free-route.

title: Aircraft Deconfliction via Mathematical Programming: Review and Insights
finder_method_summary: Survey of OR models for tactical conflict detection and resolution: unifies the different mathematical representations of pairwise separation conditions (MILP, MINLP, disjunctive, continuous-time) and revisits the models to compare their computational performance. TS 56(1):118-140.
finder_relevance_note: Reference taxonomy of separation-constraint formulations for any trajectory-level RAM flow model that must guarantee conflict-free 4D trajectories.

id: title:landings at logan airport describing and increasing airport capacity
title: Landings at Logan Airport: Describing and Increasing Airport Capacity
finder_method_summary: Empirical and optimization analysis of landing sequences at Boston Logan: statistical characterisation of interarrival separations and an optimisation of landing order/timing to increase runway throughput.

title: Solving Optimally the Static Ground-Holding Policy Problem in Air Traffic Control
finder_method_summary: Static single-airport ground-holding problem with capacity uncertainty represented by a small set of probabilistic capacity-profile scenarios over discrete time periods; aircraft aggregated into classes by scheduled arrival period; formulated as a stochastic linear program with recourse (airborne holding) whose LP solution is integer, solvable on a PC for the largest US airports; compared with deterministic and no-hold strategies across weather scenarios.
finder_relevance_note: Provides the canonical two-stage recourse template (ground hold now, airborne hold later) and the aggregate-by-period demand representation that a RAM airport-capacity model under weather uncertainty can adopt directly.

title: Strategic Flow Management for Air Traffic Control
finder_method_summary: Single-airport ground-holding problem for flights from many origins arriving at one congested airport: the deterministic case is solved as a minimum-cost network flow (assignment of flights to arrival time slots with time-varying capacity, with a simple greedy algorithm under certain cost assumptions); heuristics and dynamic programming are given for the stochastic-capacity case.
finder_relevance_note: Shows the min-cost-flow structure of single-destination hold assignment and why exact DP over capacity states explodes, motivating scenario-based or ADP approaches for RAM networks.

id: title:decomposition algorithms for analyzing transient phenomena in multiclass queueing networks
title: Decomposition Algorithms for Analyzing Transient Phenomena in Multiclass Queueing Networks, with an Application to Air Transportation
finder_method_summary: Decomposition approach for transient, time-varying multiclass queueing networks, applied to delays propagating across a network of airports with time-dependent demand and capacity.

title: The Multiple Connections Multi-Airport Ground Holding Problem: Models and Algorithms
finder_method_summary: Multi-airport ground-holding problem with multiple connections between flights (same aircraft continuing legs), formulated as an integer program over discrete time periods with airport capacity constraints and connection coupling; exact and heuristic algorithms.
finder_relevance_note: Multiple-connection structure maps to RAM aircraft rotations with several dependent legs per day and to passenger transfers at regional hubs.

title: A Comparison of Formulations for the Single-Airport Ground-Holding Problem with Banking Constraints
finder_method_summary: Builds five 0-1 IP formulations of the single-airport ground-holding problem with hub banking constraints (groups of flights must land within fixed windows), compares them analytically and computationally, proves the banking constraints induce facets for two formulations, and exploits a variable transformation and tailored branching.
finder_relevance_note: Guides the choice of slot-assignment formulation when RAM schedules at a hub-like regional airport must keep groups of connecting flights (or aircraft rotations) together.

title: Scheduling Aircraft Landings—The Static Case
finder_method_summary: Mixed-integer 0-1 formulation of the aircraft landing problem: each aircraft gets a landing time within a time window subject to sequence-dependent minimum separations; single-runway model extended to multiple runways with runway-assignment binaries. Solved by LP-based tree search with strengthened relaxations plus a heuristic; instances up to 50 aircraft and 4 runways (OR-Library benchmarks).
finder_relevance_note: The time-window plus pairwise-separation structure is the canonical building block for runway/vertiport slot assignment in a RAM flow model and maps directly onto launch-window sequencing with pad turnaround separations at a spaceport.

title: Algorithms for Scheduling Runway Operations Under Constrained Position Shifting
finder_method_summary: Runway sequencing with Constrained Position Shifting (each aircraft may move at most k positions from its FCFS order), precedence, time-window and sequence-dependent separation constraints. Scalable dynamic programming over a network whose nodes are feasible (position, k-window subsequence) states; polynomial in number of aircraft for fixed k; real-time capable prototype.
finder_relevance_note: CPS gives a tractable, equity-aware way to re-sequence small-aircraft arrivals at a regional airport or vertiport inside a larger flow model, and the same DP applies to ordering launches on a shared pad with bounded deviation from a published manifest order.

id: title:optimal selection of airport runway configurations
title: Optimal Selection of Airport Runway Configurations
finder_method_summary: Integer programming model over discrete time periods that selects the runway configuration and the arrival/departure rate point on each configuration's capacity envelope to minimise delay/configuration-change costs.

title: Queueing Models for Trajectory-Based Aircraft Operations
finder_method_summary: Single-server queue where aircraft hold scheduled times of arrival met with normally distributed error; expected queueing delay estimated by the Clark approximation, with exact results for metering at constant excess headway. Quantifies the trade-off between stochastic delay from imperfect adherence and deterministic delay from larger metered headways.
finder_relevance_note: Gives closed-form delay-versus-buffer trade-offs for 4D-trajectory RAM operations where small aircraft are metered into regional airport fixes.

title: An Integrated Scheduling and Operations Approach to Airport Congestion Mitigation
finder_method_summary: Integrates a strategic scheduling-intervention IP (displacing flights subject to airline schedule preferences and connections) with a stochastic dynamic queuing model of runway operations and a dynamic program controlling runway configurations and service rates; an iterative algorithm alternates between the two and shows large delay reductions for small displacement at JFK.
finder_relevance_note: Template for coupling a strategic RAM network flow IP with a tactical stochastic model of regional-airport/vertiport throughput via alternating decomposition.

title: A Queuing Model of the Airport Departure Process
finder_method_summary: Analytical model of the departure process: estimation of unimpeded taxi-out time distributions and a transient D(t)/Ek(t)/1 queueing model of the departure runway server; validated at Newark (EWR) and used for departure metering/pushback rate control.
finder_relevance_note: Provides the departure-server queue and metering logic for small-airport RAM operations where gate/charging-stand holds substitute for taxi queues.

title: Unified Optimization of Traffic Flows Through Airports
finder_method_summary: Integer program over a time-discretised airport network (taxiways, runways, arrival/departure fixes, gates) that jointly assigns runway configurations, sequencing and flow rates to minimise delay; large instances solved with commercial MIP after strengthening.

id: title:pruning rules for optimal runway sequencing
title: Pruning Rules for Optimal Runway Sequencing
finder_method_summary: Exact runway sequencing (take-offs and landings) with sequence-dependent separations and complex objectives; exploits problem structure through dominance and pruning rules within a dynamic-programming / tree search to solve realistic instances to optimality.
finder_relevance_note: Pruning/dominance techniques transfer to exact sequencing of mixed eVTOL and conventional arrivals at RAM airports.

title: An optimization approach for the terminal airspace scheduling problem
finder_method_summary: Joint runway sequencing and TMA control (speed, holding, vectoring, point-merge) formulated with a linear programming core embedded in a metaheuristic search; validated on Singapore Changi, reporting about 27 percent delay reduction versus baseline sequences.
finder_relevance_note: Shows how speed control and holding in terminal airspace can be co-optimised with runway slots, which is the tactical layer of a RAM flow model.

title: Scheduling of Time-Shared Jet Aircraft
finder_method_summary: Fractional-ownership jet scheduling: aircraft dispersed over locations, customer requests (origin, departure time, destination) must be served at minimum cost under maintenance and pre-scheduled trips. Shows the problem is NP-complete, gives a polynomial network-flow algorithm and a pseudo-polynomial DP for two special cases, a 0-1 integer program solved by CPLEX for small/medium instances and a fast heuristic for large ones. TS 32(3) 277-294.
finder_relevance_note: Classic pre-2005 root of on-demand small-aircraft fleet dispatch; its network-flow special cases and IP model are the template for assigning RAM aircraft to requests subject to turnaround (maintenance/charging) constraints.

id: title:per seat on demand air transportation part i problem description and an integer multicommo
title: Per-Seat, On-Demand Air Transportation Part I: Problem Description and an Integer Multicommodity Flow Model
finder_method_summary: Defines the dial-a-flight problem (on-demand per-seat air transportation with small jets between many airports) and formulates it as an integer multicommodity network flow model with side constraints on a time-expanded network of airports; each aircraft is a commodity, passenger requests with time windows ride on arcs. Part I of a two-part study; TS 42(3) 263-278.
finder_relevance_note: Direct ancestor of RAM on-demand operations: the time-space multicommodity flow with airport and aircraft constraints is the same skeleton a RAM flow model would use to assign departures, routes and holds for small aircraft across many regional airports.

id: title:per seat on demand air transportation part ii parallel local search
title: Per-Seat, On-Demand Air Transportation Part II: Parallel Local Search
finder_method_summary: Companion paper solving the large-scale dial-a-flight integer multicommodity flow model of Part I by a parallel local search that repeatedly re-optimises small subsets of aircraft/requests with an IP solver; shown to handle realistic instance sizes for a per-seat on-demand air carrier. TS 42(3) 279-291.
finder_relevance_note: Supplies the large-scale solution strategy (IP-based neighbourhood re-optimisation) that a RAM network-wide departure/route/hold assignment would need once the time-expanded model exceeds exact-solver reach.

id: title:automated flight planning of high density urban air mobility
title: Automated flight planning of high-density urban air mobility
finder_method_summary: Proposes a semi-structured UAM airspace with a layered altitude topology and direct routes between entry and exit points, and an optimisation-based automated flight-planning procedure that generates conflict-free 4D trajectories (route/layer, departure time and speed adjustments) for medium- to high-density operations; evaluated in a metropolitan case study (TR-C vol. 131, 2021).
finder_relevance_note: Strategic pre-departure 4D trajectory assignment in structured low-altitude airspace is trajectory-based ATFM for UAM; the layered route structure is a candidate airspace model for RAM corridors.

title: Development of optimal scheduling strategy and approach control model of multicopter VTOL aircrafts for urban air mobility (UAM) operation
finder_method_summary: Proposes three approach-control and arrival-scheduling strategies for multicopter VTOL aircraft at a vertiport: BQA (branch queuing approach, aircraft constrained to fixed paths), SBA (sequence-based approach with free movement) and SBAM (SBA with moving separation circles); strategies are compared by simulation on punctuality and loss-of-separation risk, with BQA found most efficient with zero LOS risk (TR-C vol. 128, art. 103181).
finder_relevance_note: Vertiport-side arrival sequencing under pad capacity is the terminal module of a RAM flow model; the queuing/sequence rules define the capacity profile the network-level model must respect.

id: title:terminal area control rules and evtol adaptive scheduling model for multi vertiport system
title: Terminal area control rules and eVTOL adaptive scheduling model for multi-vertiport system in urban air Mobility
finder_method_summary: Defines terminal-area airspace structure and control rules (approach/departure fixes, holding) for a system of several vertiports and formulates an adaptive scheduling model that assigns landing and take-off slots to eVTOLs across the vertiports subject to separation and pad capacity, minimising delay; performance is evaluated by simulation of the multi-vertiport system (TR-C vol. 132, art. 103385).
finder_relevance_note: Multi-vertiport slot scheduling with pad and separation capacity is the terminal-side building block of a RAM flow model where regional airports replace vertiports.

id: title:a space time energy flow based integer programming model to design and operate a regional
title: A space–time-energy flow-based integer programming model to design and operate a regional shared automated electric vehicle (SAEV) system and corresponding charging network
finder_method_summary: Integer program on a space-time-energy expanded network that jointly designs charging infrastructure and operates a regional shared automated electric vehicle fleet (vehicle flows with state-of-charge layers, charging arcs, demand service).
finder_relevance_note: The space-time-energy expanded network is exactly the representation needed for electric RAM flow management (and for time-expanded feeder service design with vehicle balancing).

id: title:complexity optimal air traffic assignment in multi layer transport network for urban air m
title: Complexity optimal air traffic assignment in multi-layer transport network for Urban Air Mobility operations
finder_method_summary: Macroscopic traffic assignment of UAM flows on a multi-layer corridor network that minimises congestion and an intrinsic air-traffic complexity metric based on a linear dynamical system; solved by a two-step method based on Dafermos' algorithm; two-layer case study shows congestion mitigation and low-complexity flow patterns. TR-C 142 (2022), venue from a citing paper's reference list.
finder_relevance_note: Network-level flow assignment with a complexity-based capacity proxy is strategic ATFM for UAM corridors; transfers to RAM route-network demand-capacity balancing.

id: title:complexity optimal air traffic assignment in multi layer transport networks for urban air
title: Complexity optimal air traffic assignment in multi-layer transport networks for Urban Air Mobility operations
finder_method_summary: Macroscopic static traffic assignment on a multilayer UAM route network: flows are allocated to routes to minimise a congestion factor plus intrinsic air-traffic complexity measured with a linear dynamical system (LDS) metric, solved by a two-step method based on Dafermos' algorithm; a two-layer network case study shows congestion mitigation and low-complexity flow organisation.
finder_relevance_note: The aggregate flow-assignment view is the UAM/RAM counterpart of Eulerian ATFM and DTA models and gives a strategic flow layer above flight-level time-expanded models.

id: title:integrated fleet assignment and scheduling for environmentally friendly electrified region
title: Integrated fleet assignment and scheduling for environmentally friendly electrified regional air mobility
authors: Justin, Payan, Mavris (authors per facet brief; not displayed in result)
finder_method_summary: Integrated fleet assignment and schedule optimisation for electrified regional air mobility (small electric aircraft, short routes between regional airports) with battery/charging constraints and environmental objectives; built on a US-wide RAM demand model and a fleet routing/schedule optimisation environment. TR-C 138, art. 103567 (from Georgia Tech faculty page and result text).
finder_relevance_note: The closest in-scope paper to the RAM problem statement itself: schedule and fleet assignment for small electric aircraft between many regional airports with charging/turnaround capacity.

id: title:traffic management and resource allocation for uav based parcel delivery in low altitude u
title: Traffic management and resource allocation for UAV-based parcel delivery in low-altitude urban space
finder_method_summary: Framework for UAV traffic management in low-altitude urban airspace: clustering-based UAV path planning, UTM conflict detection and resolution, and mechanism design (auction-type) for allocating scarce airspace resources among UAV operators (TR-C Oct 2022).
finder_relevance_note: Treats low-altitude drone traffic as a capacity-allocation problem, an analogue of UAM/RAM demand-capacity balancing in constrained urban airspace.

id: title:a quasi dynamic air traffic assignment model for mitigating air traffic complexity and con
title: A quasi-dynamic air traffic assignment model for mitigating air traffic complexity and congestion for high-density UAM operations
finder_method_summary: Quasi-dynamic traffic assignment (QATA) that splits the planning horizon into time slices, assigns UAM route flows per slice and propagates loading across slices (semi-dynamic loading without per-vehicle FIFO or spillback), minimising congestion plus LDS-based complexity inside a centralised strategic planning scheme; iterative assignment solved slice by slice. Corroborated only by a search summary describing the model; no page or venue string was seen.
finder_relevance_note: Adds the time dimension to aggregate UAM flow assignment, bridging dynamic traffic assignment machinery and time-expanded RAM flow scheduling.

title: Branch-and-Price for Drone Delivery Service Planning in Urban Airspace
finder_method_summary: Plans drone delivery flights within an urban UTM network modelled as airspace above the road network with multiple flight levels; drones are routed conflict-free (time-space separation) through the network and the problem is solved by branch-and-price with customised heuristics to obtain near-optimal integer solutions on realistic instances. TS 57(4) 843-865.
finder_relevance_note: Treats low-altitude drone traffic management as a capacitated time-space routing problem solved by column generation, directly transferable to RAM/UAM strategic deconfliction and pre-departure scheduling.

id: title:chance constrained uam traffic flow optimization with fast disruption recovery under uncer
title: Chance-constrained UAM traffic flow optimization with fast disruption recovery under uncertain waypoint occupancy time
finder_method_summary: Trajectory-based UAM traffic flow management: chance-constrained optimisation that assigns conflict-free 4D trajectories/waypoint occupancy times under stochastic occupancy durations, with a fast re-optimisation procedure for disruption recovery.
finder_relevance_note: Stochastic ATFM with recourse for UAM; waypoint occupancy windows are the UAM counterpart of sector/airport capacity slots.

id: title:conflict probability based strategic conflict resolution for uas traffic management consid
title: Conflict probability based strategic conflict resolution for UAS traffic management considering Reasonable-Time-To-Act principle
finder_method_summary: Strategic (pre-departure) conflict resolution for UTM: two-step detection (coarse screening then conflict-probability estimation over operational volumes) followed by resolution respecting a reasonable-time-to-act principle; operational-volume abstraction reduces computation.
finder_relevance_note: Strategic deconfliction is the UTM form of pre-departure ATFM; probabilistic capacity/occupancy treatment is relevant to RAM flow models.

id: title:on demand ridesharing based on dynamic scheduling in urban air mobility
title: On-demand ridesharing based on dynamic scheduling in urban air mobility
finder_method_summary: Integrated dynamic scheduling model for multimodal UAM ridesharing (ground legs to/from vertiports plus eVTOL legs) solved in four stages: travel service plan generation, available-resource search (improved pulse algorithm), dynamic cooperative multi-task assignment and vehicle rebalancing (hybrid adaptive large neighbourhood search). NYC experiments report about 25 percent higher service rate and 52 percent lower detour time than conventional ridesharing. TR-C, June 2025.
finder_relevance_note: Recent on-demand UAM operations model whose dynamic vehicle schedules are the demand stream a tactical RAM/UAM flow manager must deconflict.

id: title:real time traffic simulation and management for large scale urban air mobility integrating
title: Real-time traffic simulation and management for large-scale urban air mobility: Integrating route guidance and collision avoidance
finder_method_summary: Large-scale real-time UAM traffic simulation and management combining network-level route guidance (congestion-aware routing) with tactical collision avoidance; evaluates throughput and delay at city scale (arXiv 2412.01235 preprint).
finder_relevance_note: Hierarchical strategic routing + tactical separation evaluated by simulation is the standard way UAM flow management is validated; relevant to RAM test-beds.

id: title:pre planned air routes or dynamic 4d trajectories a comparative study of utm conops
title: Pre-planned air routes or dynamic 4D trajectories? A comparative study of UTM ConOps
finder_method_summary: Comparative study of UTM concepts of operation: fixed pre-planned air-route (corridor) networks versus free dynamic 4D trajectories, assessed on capacity, delay and safety via simulation/optimisation.
finder_relevance_note: Structured corridors vs free-routing is the UAM version of the fixed-route vs trajectory-based-operations question central to ATFM modelling.

title: Multicriteria Model to Determine Flight Frequencies on an Airline Network under Competitive Conditions
finder_method_summary: Nonlinear integer multicriteria model choosing route frequencies on an airline network under competition, maximizing profit and passengers carried while minimizing total passenger schedule delay; solved by Monte Carlo random generation of solutions and selection of the best (TS 23(1):14-25).
finder_relevance_note: Early frequency-design model on a route network with competition and schedule-delay objectives; the frequency decisions it makes are the demand input to a RAM flow problem.

id: title:high speed rail and air transport competition game engineering as tool for cost benefit an
title: High-speed rail and air transport competition: Game engineering as tool for cost-benefit analysis
finder_method_summary: Game-engineering methodology for infrastructure cost-benefit analysis: high-speed rail, hub-and-spoke legacy airlines and regional low-cost carriers maximize best-response functions over prices, frequencies and vehicle sizes given infrastructure, costs and environmental charges; applied to EU-27 Trans-European network corridors.
finder_relevance_note: Framework for assessing regional air services competing with high-speed rail on frequency and aircraft size, central to RAM market viability.

title: Modeling Airline Frequency Competition for Airport Congestion Mitigation
finder_method_summary: Game-theoretic model of airline frequency competition under airport slot constraints; Nash equilibrium found by successive optimizations, each solved by dynamic programming. Validated against observed frequencies; used to evaluate slot-allocation schemes, showing small slot reductions cut flight/passenger delays and raise airline profits (TS 46(4):512-535).
finder_relevance_note: Links strategic frequency choice to airport capacity and delay, the interface between RAM network planning and demand-capacity balancing at capacity-limited regional airports and vertiports.

title: A method for urban air mobility network design using hub location and subgraph isomorphism
finder_method_summary: Formulates UAM network design as a hub location problem whose candidate hub-and-spoke topologies are enumerated via subgraph isomorphism against a candidate-site graph, selecting a small set of vertiport hubs and spoke assignments to serve regional demand. Reported in TR-C vol. 125, art. 102997 (April 2021).
finder_relevance_note: Hub location over a candidate-site graph with a small hub set serving many spokes is the direct structural analog of choosing a few orbital hubs fed by many ground spaceports;

title: Are commuter air taxis coming to your city? A case study for 40 cities in the United States
finder_method_summary: Demand-side feasibility study of commuter air-taxi service across 40 US cities using commute data and time-savings/cost thresholds (TR-C 132, 2021).
finder_relevance_note: Provides the demand inputs and vertiport-pair structure for UAM/RAM flow models.

title: Urban air mobility: A comprehensive review and comparative analysis with autonomous and electric ground transportation for informing future research
finder_method_summary: Review paper (TR-C 132): surveys UAM demand, vehicle, infrastructure (vertiport), airspace/UTM and operations research streams and contrasts them with autonomous/electric ground transport; identifies open modelling questions (fleet/vertiport operations, scheduling, demand-capacity).
finder_relevance_note: Anchor review that situates UAM traffic-management and network-operations research; useful to frame the RAM ATFM extension and locate further TR-C work.

id: title:optimizing the battery charging and swapping infrastructure for electric short haul aircra
title: Optimizing the battery charging and swapping infrastructure for electric short-haul aircraft—The case of electric flight in Norway
finder_method_summary: Electric short-haul aircraft fleet scheduling with charging and battery-swapping as a MILP, embedded as a subroutine in an infrastructure-sizing problem solved by simulated annealing; Norway case shows charger/spare-battery mix lets fleets fly about three times fleet size in round trips, charging early and swapping in busy afternoons.
finder_relevance_note: Charging/turnaround capacity at regional airports is an explicit RAM flow constraint; this gives the scheduling model and sizing logic.

id: title:integrated air rail scheduling a branch and price approach for adaptive passenger centric
title: Integrated air-rail scheduling: A branch-and-price approach for adaptive passenger-centric planning
finder_method_summary: Integrated scheduling of air and rail services with passenger-centric (itinerary) objectives, solved by branch-and-price; adaptive planning across modes (from title and PII only; TR-B 2025).
finder_relevance_note: Recent TR-B treatment of air services scheduled jointly with a competing/complementary ground mode, relevant to RAM networks feeding or competing with high-speed rail.

id: title:swapping applications in a daily airline fleet assignment
title: Swapping Applications in a Daily Airline Fleet Assignment
finder_method_summary: Swap-based moves on a daily fleet assignment time-space network to restore maintenance/crew feasibility or improve cost with polynomial swap detection. IDEAS URL (TS 30(3) 237-248) seen; title from memory, not displayed in result.
finder_relevance_note: Swap operators on the time-space network are the basic recovery moves for a RAM flow re-plan.

title: Advances in the Optimization of Airline Fleet Assignment
finder_method_summary: Large-scale fleet assignment as a multicommodity flow on a per-fleet time-space (connection) network with flight-cover, flow-balance and fleet-count constraints; model enhancements (node consolidation, maintenance/crew-driven restrictions) plus LP/branch-and-bound strategies solve a USAir-scale daily problem.
finder_relevance_note: The time-space network with ground arcs and aircraft-count constraints is the canonical template for assigning a RAM fleet to legs across many regional airports.

title: On the Airline Schedule Perturbation Problem Caused by the Ground Delay Program
finder_relevance_note: Operator response to flow-management holds, relevant for RAM fleets with tight turnaround and charging chains.

title: The Aircraft Maintenance Routing Problem
finder_method_summary: Routing aircraft so that each visits a maintenance station every three days and satisfies balance-check requirements; static and dynamic models with fast polynomial-time algorithms based on Euler tours / graph structure of the line-of-flight network.
finder_relevance_note: Rotation cycles with periodic maintenance visits are the structure of reusable vehicle rotations between spaceports and refurbishment sites.

title: The Four-Day Aircraft Maintenance Routing Problem
finder_method_summary: Extends maintenance routing to a four-day visit requirement; shows NP-completeness and gives heuristics/exact approaches for constructing rotations on the daily line-of-flight graph; TS 32(1):43-53.
finder_relevance_note: Complexity boundary for periodic asset-cycle constraints informs how reusable-vehicle turnaround rules should be modelled.

title: Airline Fleet Assignment with Time Windows
finder_method_summary: Generalised FAM that assigns fleet types and simultaneously chooses departure times: each flight gets a time window discretised into flight copies on the time-space network; a direct solution approach and an iterative memory-saving approach solve real large-scale instances with lower cost and tighter schedules.
finder_relevance_note: Discrete departure-time copies within windows is exactly how launch-window choice (B) or RAM departure-time assignment (A) can be embedded in a fleet/vehicle assignment model.

title: Benders Decomposition for Simultaneous Aircraft Routing and Crew Scheduling
finder_method_summary: Integrated aircraft routing and crew pairing with linking (short-connection) constraints; Benders decomposition iterating between a routing master and a crew-pairing subproblem, each solved by column generation; cost reductions versus sequential planning.
finder_relevance_note: Benders between two column-generation problems is a reusable pattern for coupling vehicle rotations with a second resource (crews, pads, recovery ships).

title: Itinerary-Based Airline Fleet Assignment
finder_method_summary: Extends leg-based FAM to itinerary-level passenger demand with spill and recapture (IFAM): a MIP coupling time-space fleet flows with passenger itinerary flows, solved by combined row and column generation; shows revenue gains over leg-based FAM on major US airline data.
finder_relevance_note: Couples capacity assignment on the time-space network to O-D passenger flows, the structure needed to size RAM aircraft to multi-leg regional itineraries.

title: Applications of Operations Research in the Air Transport Industry
finder_method_summary: Survey of OR in air transport: schedule planning (schedule design, fleet assignment, routing, crew), revenue management, and aviation infrastructure planning and operations (airport/airspace capacity, ATFM); historical perspective and state of the art.
finder_relevance_note: Anchor review connecting airline-side time-space scheduling with airport/airspace capacity management for both topics.

title: Improving Crew Scheduling by Incorporating Key Maintenance Routing Decisions
