finder_method_summary: Extended crew pairing model that embeds only the maintenance routing decisions that matter for crews (short connections), using composite 'routing solution' variables to keep the integrated problem tractable; OR 51(3):387-396 per search summary.
finder_relevance_note: Composite-variable integration of a vehicle-routing layer into a resource-covering layer is reusable for coupling RAM aircraft rotations with pilot/charger resources.

title: Rerouting Aircraft for Airline Recovery
finder_method_summary: Aircraft recovery as a set-packing model over candidate aircraft routes with cancellations and delays; an aircraft-selection heuristic restricts rerouting to a small subset so the MIP stays tractable; evaluated with SimAir, showing large savings over simple strategies.
finder_relevance_note: Restricting re-optimisation to a chosen subset of vehicles is a scalable pattern for rolling-horizon RAM recovery.

title: A Robust Fleet-Assignment Model with Hub Isolation and Short Cycles
finder_method_summary: Modifies FAM to generate rotations with many short cycles and low hub connectivity so cancellations and swaps remain local; evaluated with the SimAir simulation; better recovery at small planning-cost increase.
finder_relevance_note: Short-cycle rotations contain delay propagation across a many-airport regional network.

title: Airline Schedule Planning: Integrated Models and Algorithms for Schedule Design and Fleet Assignment
finder_method_summary: Integrated schedule design and fleet assignment: mixed-integer model that selects which optional flight legs to operate and assigns fleet types while capturing demand recapture/spill across itineraries (itinerary-based fleet assignment with demand corrections). Solved with column/row generation on a time-space network per fleet; demonstrated on a major US airline's schedule (TS 38(1):19-32).
finder_relevance_note: The time-space fleet network with leg selection and aircraft-size choice is the template for deciding which regional legs an electric fleet flies and with what capacity before flow management.

title: Polyhedral Analysis and Algorithms for a Demand-Driven Refleeting Model for Aircraft Assignment
finder_method_summary: MIP for demand-driven refleeting: dynamically reassigning aircraft capacities within a fleet family close to departure as demand forecasts improve, maximising revenue; polyhedral study yields tightened reformulations and valid inequalities; tested on United Airlines instances.
finder_relevance_note: Late capacity re-assignment as forecasts sharpen transfers to RAM aircraft-size swaps (A) and reallocation of launch-vehicle capacity among spokes (B).

title: Planning for Robust Airline Operations: Optimizing Aircraft Routings and Flight Departure Times to Minimize Passenger Disruptions
finder_method_summary: Two models: robust aircraft routing minimising expected propagated delay with a string-based stochastic MIP solved by branch-and-price, and flight retiming within small time windows to minimise misconnecting passengers; real data show large reductions in propagated delay and disruptions.
finder_relevance_note: Retiming within windows and slack placement along rotations are the levers a RAM flow model needs to protect tight turnaround/charging buffers.

title: Integrated Airline Fleeting and Crew-Pairing Decisions
finder_method_summary: Integrates fleet assignment with crew pairing (bypassing routing through plane-count constraints); two solution methods, Lagrangian relaxation with column generation and Benders decomposition; results on a major airline.
finder_relevance_note: Plane-count constraints as a proxy for routing feasibility is a lightweight way to keep RAM vehicle-balance constraints in an integrated model.

title: Incorporating Network Flow Effects into the Airline Fleet Assignment Process
finder_relevance_note: Decomposition that couples a capacity-assignment MIP with a flow/revenue subproblem suits vehicle-to-window assignment with payload flow valuation.

title: Airline Fleet Assignment with Enhanced Revenue Modeling
finder_method_summary: Fleet assignment with a subnetwork-based revenue model that approximates itinerary-level spill and recapture more accurately than leg-based models while keeping tractability; DOI quoted in a search summary (Articles in Advance 2008, print 2009).
finder_relevance_note: Intermediate-granularity demand modelling between leg and full itinerary is useful when payload demand is defined by origin-destination-orbit groups.

title: Dynamic Airline Scheduling
finder_method_summary: Re-times flights and re-fleets during the booking period as demand information updates, preserving connectivity and aircraft balance on a time-space network with flight copies; MIP shows profit gains over a static schedule.
finder_relevance_note: Rolling re-timing/re-fleeting as information arrives is the planning-side analogue of a dynamic RAM flow re-plan (A) and of re-slotting launches as manifests firm up (B).

id: title:improving the objective function of the fleet assignment problem
title: Improving the objective function of the fleet assignment problem
finder_method_summary: Iteratively improves the fleet assignment objective by alternating between generating fleet assignments and analysing them with a modified passenger flow model, correcting leg-based revenue estimates that ignore multileg itinerary interdependence; TR-B 43(4):466-475.
finder_relevance_note: Iterative assignment-evaluation loop is a practical way to couple a vehicle-window assignment MIP with a payload flow simulator.

title: Integrated Airline Fleet and Crew Robust Planning
finder_method_summary: Integrates fleet assignment and crew planning with station-purity/crew-base restrictions to limit crew connections and improve robustness; decomposition-based solution. From title/venue seen; details from known paper.
finder_relevance_note: Purity constraints limiting vehicle types per station translate to limiting vehicle classes per spaceport for ground-support simplicity.

title: An Optimization Approach to Airline Integrated Recovery
finder_method_summary: Fully integrated recovery of schedule, aircraft, crew and passengers via Benders decomposition with a schedule-recovery master and aircraft/crew/passenger subproblems using column generation; single-day horizon on a US hub-and-spoke carrier; first computational results for the fully integrated problem.
finder_relevance_note: Decomposition architecture for re-planning a flow schedule with coupled resources after disruption.

title: Robust Airline Schedule Planning: Minimizing Propagated Delay in an Integrated Routing and Crewing Framework
finder_method_summary: Computes propagated delay jointly along aircraft routes and crew pairings; iterative algorithm alternating routing and crew column generation with updated propagated-delay costs; real network data show lower propagated delay than sequential planning.
finder_relevance_note: Delay-propagation accounting across coupled resources is needed when RAM aircraft and pilots share tight regional rotations.

title: A Lifted Compact Formulation for the Daily Aircraft Maintenance Routing Problem
finder_method_summary: Compact polynomial-size MIP for daily maintenance routing strengthened by lifting / RLT-based valid inequalities, solving large instances to optimality without column generation; TS 47(4):508-525.
finder_relevance_note: Compact lifted formulations are an alternative to string-based branch-and-price for vehicle rotation cycles.

title: A Network-Based Model for the Integrated Weekly Aircraft Maintenance Routing and Fleet Assignment Problem
finder_method_summary: Weekly rotation-tour network representation yielding a compact MILP (WRTNM) whose size grows linearly with the weekly schedule and has a very tight LP relaxation; integrated with fleet assignment; optimal solutions for 5,700 flights and 330 aircraft within five minutes; TS 47(4):493-507.
finder_relevance_note: Shows how periodic service constraints (charging, inspection) can be enforced with flow constraints rather than route enumeration in a RAM time-space model.

title: An Integrated Approach for Airline Flight Selection and Timing, Fleet Assignment, and Aircraft Routing
finder_method_summary: Integrated MIP covering selection and re-timing of optional flights, fleet assignment and aircraft (maintenance) routing with itinerary-based demand; solved with Benders decomposition and lifting; matches TS 47(4):455-476 IDEAS entry.
finder_relevance_note: Fully integrated choose-time-assign-route model is the most complete analog for launch window selection plus vehicle assignment plus rotation.

id: title:cruise speed reduction for ground delay programs a case study for san francisco internatio
title: Cruise speed reduction for ground delay programs: A case study for San Francisco International Airport arrivals
finder_method_summary: Aircraft-performance trajectory model that computes the 'equivalent cruise speed' (slower speed with the same fuel burn as nominal cruise) so that GDP-assigned delay is absorbed airborne and remains recoverable if the GDP is cancelled early; recoverable delay is quantified against flight length, aircraft type and cancellation time on SFO arrivals. DOI not seen; already in the A1 verified pipeline.
finder_relevance_note: Supplies the speed-versus-energy feasibility envelope a RAM flow model needs to price airborne delay absorption for small electric aircraft (battery-equivalent speed in place of fuel-equivalent speed).

title: Integrated Flight Scheduling and Fleet Assignment Under Airport Congestion
finder_method_summary: Integrated flight scheduling and fleet assignment MIP that maximizes expected airline profit while internalizing aircraft and passenger delay costs at congested, slot-constrained airports; delays are modeled as functions of scheduled demand versus capacity and embedded in the schedule-design network (TS 47(4):477-492).
finder_relevance_note: Endogenous congestion/delay costs at capacity-limited nodes connect airline schedule design to ATFM demand-capacity balancing (A) and to hub-capacity-aware launch scheduling (B).

title: Aircraft Rescheduling with Cruise Speed Control
finder_method_summary: Recovery MIP choosing cruise speeds (nonlinear fuel and emission costs) together with aircraft swaps and delays to absorb disruptions; conic quadratic mixed-integer reformulation; first model with speed as an explicit recovery decision under environmental costs.
finder_relevance_note: Conic reformulation of speed-energy tradeoffs is the modelling route for battery-energy-vs-block-time decisions in RAM recovery.

id: title:operating cost based cruise speed reduction for ground delay programs effect of scope leng
title: Operating cost based cruise speed reduction for ground delay programs: Effect of scope length
finder_method_summary: Extends the cruise-speed-reduction GDP strategy with a cost-index (airline operating-cost) speed criterion and a parametric analysis of GDP scope length, i.e. which flights are included and hence how long they are airborne, trading controller commitment under uncertainty against airline cost. DOI not seen; already in the A1 verified pipeline.
finder_relevance_note: Shows how the geographic scope of a flow-control programme interacts with speed control; for RAM the analogue is deciding which regional feeder legs are long enough to absorb delay airborne rather than on the ground or at a charger.

id: title:the recoverable robust tail assignment problem
title: The Recoverable Robust Tail Assignment Problem
finder_method_summary: Recoverable-robust tail assignment as a two-stage stochastic program (planning plus recovery scenarios with cancellation, delay and swap options and passenger rerouting cost); Benders decomposition with column generation in master and subproblems; lower recovery costs shown.
finder_relevance_note: Tail assignment with explicit recovery recourse maps to assigning reusable launch vehicles with recourse for scrubs (B) and RAM tail assignment under charging/weather disruptions (A).

title: A math-heuristic algorithm for the integrated air service recovery
finder_method_summary: Integrated aircraft, crew and passenger recovery solved by a math-heuristic that iterates between MIP stages on time-band/flight-copy networks. DOI quoted in search summary (no page URL seen); details
finder_relevance_note: Staged matheuristic is a practical route to fast RAM recovery when a monolithic model is too large.

title: Airline-Driven Performance-Based Air Traffic Management: Game Theoretic Models and Multicriteria Evaluation
finder_method_summary: Proposes mechanisms (averaging, voting, ranking variants) to collect airline inputs and aggregate them into implementable ATM initiatives, with a game-theoretic analysis of strategic gaming by airlines and a multicriteria evaluation of outcomes.
finder_relevance_note: Preference-aggregation mechanisms for setting flow-management objectives across heterogeneous RAM operators, with gaming analysis.

title: Solving the Integrated Airline Recovery Problem Using Column-and-Row Generation
finder_method_summary: Integrated schedule, crew and aircraft recovery in one model solved by column-and-row generation (linking rows added dynamically), reducing problem size and improving runtime and solution quality over standard column generation.
finder_relevance_note: Column-and-row generation is a reusable large-scale method for RAM recovery models with dynamically generated coupling constraints.

title: Flight Network-Based Approach for Integrated Airline Recovery with Cruise Speed Control
finder_method_summary: New flight-network representation of integrated recovery for aircraft, crew and passengers with delays, rerouting, cancellations and cruise-speed decisions; conic quadratic MIP solved in reasonable time for practical instances.
finder_relevance_note: Flow-of-entities network with speed decisions is a compact alternative to flight-copy networks for RAM recovery.

id: title:integrated disruption management and flight planning to trade off delays and fuel burn
title: Integrated Disruption Management and Flight Planning to Trade Off Delays and Fuel Burn
finder_method_summary: Integrates flight planning (cruise speed choice) with schedule recovery (holds, swaps, cancellations) on a time-space recovery network with multiple flight copies per leg encoding speed/time options; MIP minimising fuel plus passenger-delay cost; 66-83% fewer passenger disruptions for about 0.15% extra fuel.
finder_relevance_note: Speed as a recourse encoded via flight copies gives the RAM flow model an energy-vs-time lever directly comparable with ATFM speed control.

title: Robust Aircraft Routing
finder_method_summary: Robust optimisation of aircraft routing minimising worst-case total propagated delay over a budgeted uncertainty set that captures correlated leg delays (weather, ATM initiatives); reformulation and decomposition algorithm; real airline data.
finder_relevance_note: Correlated-delay uncertainty sets link ATFM-induced delays to airline routing robustness, directly transferable to RAM rotations under weather.

title: Stochastic Optimization Models for Transferring Delay Along Flight Trajectories to Reduce Fuel Usage
finder_method_summary: Two-stage stochastic integer program over ground-delay-program cancellation-time scenarios in which part of each flight's assigned ground delay is converted into en-route cruise-speed reduction, so that if the GDP ends early the flight can accelerate and recover delay at no extra fuel burn relative to the ground-hold baseline. Expected fuel use is traded against expected delay on realistic GDP instances.
finder_relevance_note: Treats airborne speed reduction as a continuous recourse that shifts delay between ground and air; a RAM flow model can use the same lever when charging or airport capacity recovers earlier than forecast, with an energy-time rather than fuel-time trade-off.

title: Airline Timetable Development and Fleet Assignment Incorporating Passenger Choice
finder_method_summary: Integrated timetable development and fleet assignment with a passenger choice (discrete choice) demand model; nonlinear integer program solved by an iterative decomposition / linearization scheme with convergence results; demonstrated on an airline network.
finder_relevance_note: Choice-based demand responding to schedule times is the analog of shippers choosing among launch windows/hubs based on timing.

title: Dynamic Disruption Management in Airline Networks Under Airport Operating Uncertainty
finder_method_summary: Stochastic reactive-and-proactive disruption management combining a stochastic queuing model of hub airport congestion, a flight-planning tool and an IP for airline recovery; anticipating probabilistic future delays cuts expected recovery cost 1-2%, largely via deliberate departure holds.
finder_relevance_note: Explicitly links airport-capacity uncertainty (the ATFM input) to airline-side holds, the natural coupling for a RAM flow model.

id: title:integrated flight scheduling and fleet assignment with improved supply demand interactions
title: Integrated Flight Scheduling and Fleet Assignment with Improved Supply-Demand Interactions
finder_method_summary: Integrated flight scheduling and fleet assignment with an improved representation of supply-demand interactions (itinerary attractiveness depending on schedule); title seen on a ranking page and an IDEAS TR-B 149:162-180 entry in the same result set.
finder_relevance_note: Recent integrated schedule/fleet design with endogenous demand, a direct basis for RAM network scheduling with demand feedback.

title: Choice-Based Airline Schedule Design and Fleet Assignment: A Decomposition Approach
finder_method_summary: Integrated schedule design (selecting from optional flights) and fleet assignment with a passenger choice model over fare products; decomposition partitions the flight network into subnetworks solved and recombined; TS 56(6):1410-1431.
finder_relevance_note: Recent template for embedding demand response in time-expanded schedule/fleet design, relevant to RAM demand modelling and feeder service design.

title: Hub Network Design Problem with Capacity, Congestion, and Stochastic Demand Considerations
finder_method_summary: Generalises hub location with capacity acquisition, convex congestion costs at hubs, stochastic demand and dynamic O-D routing; path-based mixed-integer SOCP formulation, with SOCP duality giving an exact Benders decomposition plus column generation; shows congestion, uncertainty and complete vs incomplete hub graphs change designs materially (TS 57(5):1276-1295).
finder_relevance_note: Capacitated, congestion-aware hub design under demand uncertainty is the closest hub-location analogue to orbital hubs with limited launch capacity.

title: Passenger-Centric Integrated Airline Schedule and Aircraft Recovery
finder_method_summary: Integrated schedule and aircraft recovery with explicit passenger itinerary reaccommodation on a flight-copy time-space network; MIP with decomposition for large instances. From title/venue seen; details from known paper.
finder_relevance_note: Recent passenger-centred recovery template for RAM where passenger re-accommodation across small aircraft dominates cost.

title: Large-Scale Airline Crew Recovery Using Mixed-Integer Optimization and Supervised Machine Learning
finder_method_summary: Large-scale crew recovery via MIP with supervised machine learning to predict and prune candidate variables;
finder_relevance_note: ML-pruned MIP is a recent large-scale solution device applicable to RAM resource recovery.

id: title:constructing maximal dynamic flows from static flows
title: Constructing Maximal Dynamic Flows from Static Flows
finder_method_summary: Origin of flows over time: a maximal dynamic (s-t) flow over a horizon is obtained from a static min-cost flow by temporal repetition, avoiding the time-expanded network. Title taken from result summary (IDEAS record for OR 6(3) 419-433 seen).
finder_relevance_note: Foundational result that time-expanded networks can sometimes be bypassed; temporally repeated flows mirror periodic launch windows and repeating RAM schedules.

id: title:an algorithm for universal maximal dynamic flows in a network
title: An Algorithm for Universal Maximal Dynamic Flows in a Network
finder_method_summary: Earliest-arrival (universal maximal) dynamic flow algorithm: a flow over time that is maximal at every intermediate time.
finder_relevance_note: Earliest-arrival flows underpin evacuation and SO-DTA equivalences later used for capacity-constrained flow scheduling.

title: Temporal Expansion of a Transportation Network—I
finder_method_summary: Model for the optimal timing of investments in transportation network capacity over a finite planning horizon (temporal expansion);
finder_relevance_note: Multi-period capacity expansion of a network is the planning layer for adding spaceport/hub capacity as demand grows.

title: Temporal Expansion of a Transportation Network—II
finder_method_summary: Early model of scheduling link/capacity additions to a transportation network over time as demand grows (temporal network expansion). From title only.
finder_relevance_note: Capacity-timing with usage feedback relates to phasing hub/spaceport capacity against uncertain feeder demand.

title: On Multi-Commodity Maximal Dynamic Flows
finder_method_summary: Extends Ford-Fulkerson maximal dynamic flows to several commodities; examines when temporally repeated static flows remain optimal in the multicommodity case;
finder_relevance_note: Multicommodity flows over time are the aggregate form of ATFM rerouting models (Bertsimas and Stock Patterson 2000) and of multi-payload feeder flows.

id: title:a model and an algorithm for the dynamic traffic assignment problems
title: A Model and an Algorithm for the Dynamic Traffic Assignment Problems
finder_method_summary: Discrete-time, single-destination, system-optimal DTA: node demands routed through links whose per-period outflow is an exit function of occupancy; nonconvex NLP whose piecewise-linear version has staircase structure and is solved to global optimum by a one-pass simplex.
finder_relevance_note: The original time-discretised system-optimal flow model; its holding/exit-function structure is the ancestor of time-indexed ATFM capacity constraints.

id: title:optimality conditions for a dynamic traffic assignment model
title: Optimality Conditions for a Dynamic Traffic Assignment Model
finder_method_summary: Necessary optimality conditions for the Merchant-Nemhauser model: equalisation of marginal costs over used paths, generalising static assignment conditions.
finder_relevance_note: Marginal-cost interpretation of time-varying flows informs pricing/equity analysis of ATFM delay allocation.

id: title:a constraint qualification for a dynamic traffic assignment model
title: A Constraint Qualification for a Dynamic Traffic Assignment Model
finder_method_summary: Resolves whether the Merchant-Nemhauser DTA model satisfies a constraint qualification, validating the earlier optimality analysis.
finder_relevance_note: Technical underpinning of the SO-DTA lineage that ATFM time-expanded models inherit.

id: title:optimal time varying flows on congested networks
title: Optimal Time-Varying Flows on Congested Networks
finder_method_summary: Convex programming reformulation of least-cost time-varying flows on congested networks with flow-dependent arc traversal times (relaxing Merchant-Nemhauser exit-function equalities to inequalities), making the SO-DTA convex and solvable by standard methods.
finder_relevance_note: Convexification by relaxing flow-propagation equalities is the same device behind LP relaxations of time-indexed ATFM models.

id: title:dynamic network traffic assignment considered as a continuous time optimal control problem
title: Dynamic Network Traffic Assignment Considered as a Continuous Time Optimal Control Problem
finder_relevance_note: Continuous-time counterpart to discrete time-expanded models; frames the continuous-versus-discrete-time question for RAM flow models.

id: title:nonconvexity of the dynamic traffic assignment problem
title: Nonconvexity of the dynamic traffic assignment problem
finder_method_summary: Shows that the FIFO requirement yields a nonconvex constraint set in dynamic assignment, especially with multiple destinations/commodities, identifying a central difficulty for multicommodity flows over time.
finder_relevance_note: Explains why flight-level (per-commodity) integer formulations are preferred over aggregate FIFO-consistent flows in ATFM and RAM.

id: title:a new class of instantaneous dynamic user optimal traffic assignment models
title: A New Class of Instantaneous Dynamic User-Optimal Traffic Assignment Models
finder_method_summary: Defines instantaneous dynamic user-optimal assignment and formulates two models via optimal control theory for congested networks.
finder_relevance_note: Part of the OR DTA lineage whose time-discretised versions share machinery with time-expanded ATFM.

title: A Variational Inequality Formulation of the Dynamic Network User Equilibrium Problem
finder_method_summary: First VI formulation of dynamic user equilibrium with simultaneous route and departure-time choice that preserves FIFO; continuous-time infinite-dimensional VI.
finder_relevance_note: Departure-time choice under congestion is the user-side counterpart of centrally assigned ground delays in ATFM/RAM.

id: title:the cell transmission model a dynamic representation of highway traffic consistent with th
title: The cell transmission model: A dynamic representation of highway traffic consistent with the hydrodynamic theory
finder_method_summary: Discretises a link into cells and time into steps; cell-to-cell flows follow sending/receiving (min) rules consistent with LWR hydrodynamics, generating shockwaves automatically. Basis for cell-based linear SO-DTA.
finder_relevance_note: The cell/time discretisation is the ground-traffic template for Eulerian/cell-based air traffic flow models and for capacity-propagating airspace flow models.

id: title:a discrete time nested cost operator approach to the dynamic network user equilibrium prob
title: A Discrete Time, Nested Cost Operator Approach to the Dynamic Network User Equilibrium Problem
finder_method_summary: Discrete-time dynamic user equilibrium with a nested path-cost operator and heuristic solution on a time-discretised network;
finder_relevance_note: Discrete-time DUE computation on time-expanded path sets parallels time-indexed route/slot assignment.

title: The Cell Transmission Model, Part II: Network Traffic
finder_method_summary: Extends the cell transmission model to networks: predicts multi-commodity flow evolution with a macroscopic representation consistent with kinematic wave theory; models three-legged junctions and gives a numerical procedure given a time-varying OD table and known turning proportions.
finder_relevance_note: Network CTM is embedded in the LP SO-DTA models that mirror time-expanded airspace flow formulations.

title: Railway timetabling using Lagrangian relaxation
finder_method_summary: Time-discretised track-occupancy model where capacity constraints are dualised by Lagrangian relaxation so each train becomes a shortest path in a time-expanded network; TS 32(4) 358-369 per citing-paper reference list. Co-authors from recollection.
finder_relevance_note: Capacity-constrained flow scheduling over time by dualising per-period resource constraints is directly reusable for airport/sector capacities and launch-pad/hub slots.

id: title:the continuous dynamic network loading problem a mathematical formulation and solution met
title: The continuous dynamic network loading problem: A mathematical formulation and solution method
finder_method_summary: Formulates continuous dynamic network loading (temporal arc volumes, arc and path travel times given time-dependent path flows) as a system of functional equations, shows FIFO under a reasonable assumption, and develops a polynomial approximation yielding a finite-dimensional system solved as a (possibly nonsmooth) optimization problem.
finder_relevance_note: Continuous-time network loading theory for propagating time-dependent flows through a congested network.

title: Advances in the Continuous Dynamic Network Loading Problem
finder_relevance_note: Continuation of the continuous DNL theory line.

title: A Linear Programming Model for the Single Destination System Optimum Dynamic Traffic Assignment Problem
finder_method_summary: Embeds a relaxed cell transmission model in an LP over a cell-time grid to solve single-destination SO-DTA; relaxation of the min operator yields linear constraints (and the holding-back artefact).
finder_relevance_note: Canonical LP-over-time-expanded-grid formulation; the airspace analogue is an Eulerian cell-based ATFM LP.

id: title:an approach to modelling time varying flows on congested networks
title: An approach to modelling time-varying flows on congested networks
finder_method_summary: Time-expanded network model of time-varying congested flows with flow-dependent link travel times handled by discretised time intervals; title inferred from the IDEAS record (TR-B 34(8) 625-644) seen in results.
finder_relevance_note: Direct precedent for discretised time-expanded flow models with capacity and travel-time coupling.

id: title:a cell based simultaneous route and departure time choice model with elastic demand
title: A cell-based simultaneous route and departure time choice model with elastic demand
finder_method_summary: Variational inequality formulation of simultaneous route and departure-time choice with elastic demand following the ideal DUO principle, encapsulating a network cell transmission model; correctly resolves DUO under queue spillback and junction blockage and shows OD FIFO holds only under certain cost conditions.
finder_relevance_note: Cell-based dynamic equilibrium with departure-time choice is a methodological reference for time-slot/route choice in air traffic flow models.

title: Analysis of Dynamic Traffic Equilibrium with Departure Time Choice
finder_method_summary: Analytical dynamic equilibrium with departure-time choice under deterministic queueing; authors and year from recollection (only title and DOI shown in result).
finder_relevance_note: Departure-time equilibrium at a capacity bottleneck is the behavioural counterpart to assigned departure slots at a capacity-limited vertiport/airport.

title: Convergence of a Discretised Travel-Time Model
finder_relevance_note: Companion theory to discretised link travel-time models in time-expanded flow formulations.

title: A Network Flow Algorithm for the Cell-Based Single-Destination System Optimal Dynamic Traffic Assignment Problem
finder_method_summary: Shows the CTM-based single-destination SO-DTA LP is equivalent to an earliest arrival flow problem and solves it with a network-flow algorithm that avoids the vehicle-holding artefacts of simplex/interior-point solutions.
finder_relevance_note: Bridges flows-over-time theory (earliest arrival) and cell-based SO-DTA, the two pillars of this facet.

id: title:a cell based merchant nemhauser model for the system optimum dynamic traffic assignment pr
title: A cell-based Merchant-Nemhauser model for the system optimum dynamic traffic assignment problem
finder_method_summary: Proposes a cell-based variant of the Merchant-Nemhauser model for SO-DTA; once linearized and augmented with cross-cell interaction constraints it becomes an LP embedding a relaxed cell transmission model. Shows CTM dynamics derive from M-N with a suitable exit-flow function; uniform treatment of cells/intersections; an algorithm addresses the flow holding-back problem.
finder_relevance_note: System-optimal dynamic flow LP with CTM dynamics is the ground-traffic analogue of network ATFM flow models.

id: title:discretised link travel time models based on cumulative flows formulations and properties
title: Discretised link travel time models based on cumulative flows: Formulations and properties
finder_method_summary: Piecewise-linearizes cumulative inflow/outflow curves using step-function (SF) and linear-interpolation (LI) approximations to derive discretised link travel time models that ensure FIFO and continuity of travel times in flows; a modified LI model restores causality and strong FIFO.
finder_relevance_note: Cumulative-flow (by-time) variables are exactly the encoding of Bertsimas-Stock Patterson ATFM models; this paper studies their discretisation properties.

id: title:on the holding back problem in the cell transmission based dynamic traffic assignment mode
title: On the holding-back problem in the cell transmission based dynamic traffic assignment models
finder_method_summary: Analyses the artificial holding-back of vehicles in relaxed-CTM SO-DTA LPs (vehicles held despite downstream capacity) and proposes formulations/conditions to eliminate it.
finder_relevance_note: Holding-back is the artefact a time-indexed ATFM LP relaxation can exhibit when flow may be delayed for free; relevant to RAM flow LPs with holding arcs.

id: title:dynamic allocation and benefit assessment of nextgen flow corridors
title: Dynamic allocation and benefit assessment of NextGen flow corridors
finder_method_summary: Flow-based modelling identifies candidate airspace for high-density flow corridors (long narrow trajectory-based tubes), builds a corridor network mimicking user-preferred trajectories, dynamically allocates corridors and assesses benefits in complexity reduction and capacity. TR-C 33:297-310.
finder_relevance_note: Corridor networks are a direct analogue for structured RAM/UAM routes between regional airports; the allocation model informs route-capacity constraints.

title: On the System Optimum Dynamic Traffic Assignment and Earliest Arrival Flow Problems
finder_method_summary: Investigates CTM-based single-destination SO-DTA and shows backward propagation of congestion does not affect the optimal arrival flow pattern, linking SO-DTA to earliest arrival flows; authors from recollection.
finder_relevance_note: Supports using earliest-arrival flow algorithms for capacity-constrained arrival scheduling over time.

title: The Continuous-Time Service Network Design Problem
finder_method_summary: Introduces dynamic discretization discovery (DDD): a fixed-charge capacitated multicommodity flow IP is solved on a partially time-expanded network whose arcs under-estimate travel times (valid lower bound), the relaxed solution is repaired into a continuous-time-feasible plan (upper bound), and time points are added only where the relaxation is time-inconsistent; proven to converge to an exact continuous-time optimum without a fine uniform grid.
finder_relevance_note: Both the RAM departure-time/holding problem and spaceport feeder schedule design are hurt by fine time grids; DDD keeps exact continuous-time timing while using only the time points that matter.

title: Link-Based System Optimum Dynamic Traffic Assignment Problems in General Networks
finder_relevance_note: Recent OR treatment of multi-OD system-optimal flows over time, the aggregate form of network-wide ATFM.

title: Enhanced Dynamic Discretization Discovery for the Continuous Time Load Plan Design Problem
finder_method_summary: Strengthens DDD for the continuous-time load plan design (consolidation network) problem with improved relaxations, refinement rules and primal heuristics on partially time-expanded networks;
finder_relevance_note: Shows how DDD is tuned for consolidation networks, the analogue of consolidating regional payloads onto scheduled launch vehicles or feeder flights.

title: Dynamic Discretization Discovery for Solving the Time-Dependent Traveling Salesman Problem with Time Windows
finder_method_summary: Exact DDD algorithm for the TSP with hard time windows and time-dependent (FIFO) travel times: an IP relaxation on a partially time-expanded network with travel-time-under-estimating arcs gives lower bounds, infeasible tours are repaired for upper bounds, and time points are added where the relaxation is inaccurate, exploiting piecewise-linear travel-time structure.
finder_relevance_note: RAM routes have congestion-dependent (time-dependent) transit times and slot time windows at regional airports; this shows DDD handles both exactly.

title: Dynamic discretization discovery for the service network design problem with mixed autonomous fleets
finder_method_summary: Scheduled SND for city parcel logistics where level-4 autonomous vehicles must be platooned by manned vehicles outside feasible zones (vehicle synchronization); DDD on partially time-expanded networks with relaxation-based enhancements and heuristic restrictions outperforms a commercial solver.
finder_relevance_note: Fleet-mix plus scheduled-service design on a time-expanded network is the template for electric/hybrid RAM fleets and for reusable launch-vehicle fleets with turnaround constraints.

title: Interval-Based Dynamic Discretization Discovery for Solving the Continuous-Time Service Network Design Problem
finder_method_summary: Continuous-time SND solved on a partially time-expanded network by interval-based dynamic discretization discovery: each iteration solves a small IP on a coarse time-expanded network that yields a lower bound, checks whether the solution is implementable in continuous time, and refines node time intervals only where needed, converging to a provably optimal continuous-time plan. Computations show models smaller than 1% of a full time-expanded network suffice.
finder_relevance_note: Interval-based discretization is the natural fit for RAM flow holds and spaceport launch windows, where feasibility is defined over time intervals rather than instants.

id: title:new formulations for the scheduled service network design problem
title: New formulations for the Scheduled Service Network Design Problem
finder_method_summary: Formulates the SSNDP with enumerated consolidations of shipments routed on the physical network instead of a time-expanded network; stronger LP relaxation, less symmetry and much faster solution with an off-the-shelf solver.
finder_relevance_note: Formulation choices for time-expanded SND carry directly to scheduled feeder (launch) networks and scheduled RAM services.

title: Cost Function Approximation for the Dynamic Scheduled Service Network Design Problem
finder_method_summary: Dynamic (rolling, uncertain-demand) scheduled service network design on a time-expanded network solved via cost-function-approximation policies; from title only. Year inferred from manuscript number.
finder_relevance_note: Recent (2025) treatment of dynamic scheduled network design under uncertainty, relevant to rolling RAM schedule updates and to launch-manifest planning with uncertain payload demand.

title: Cross-Dock Trailer Scheduling with Workforce Constraints: A Dynamic Discretization Discovery Approach
finder_method_summary: Trailer scheduling at cross-dock doors with workforce constraints formulated on a time-expanded network and solved with DDD; outperforms full time-expanded MIP on instances with 180 trailers and ~100 doors.
finder_relevance_note: Capacity-constrained scheduling of arrivals/departures at a hub with limited handling resources is the structure of vertiport/spaceport turnaround capacity.

id: title:the location of interacting hub facilities
title: The Location of Interacting Hub Facilities
finder_method_summary: Seminal paper (TS 20(2):92-106) introducing the hub location problem: planar one- and two-hub models in which all origin-destination interactions are routed via hubs with a discounted inter-hub link, minimizing total weighted distance; solved with iterative continuous-location heuristics and illustrated on US air passenger interactions. Index page corroborates venue/pages; title and author from the search summary's reference to the 1986 Transportation Science seminal paper.
finder_relevance_note: Origin of the spoke-hub-hub-spoke cost structure; the continuous version is useful for first-cut reasoning about where a small number of transfer nodes (orbital hubs) should sit relative to a dispersed demand field of spaceports.

id: title:direct versus terminal freight routing on a network with concave costs
title: Direct versus terminal freight routing on a network with concave costs
finder_method_summary: Procedure for deciding whether a shipment should be routed through an intermediate terminal or directly to its destination on a network with concave (economies-of-scale) costs (TR-B 21(4):287-298).
finder_relevance_note: The spoke-level decision of hub routing versus direct launch under concave launch-cost curves.

title: The Break-Bulk Role of Terminals in Many-to-Many Logistic Networks
finder_method_summary: Continuum-approximation analysis of terminals as break-bulk/swapping points in many-to-many networks; quantifies benefits and disadvantages of routing vehicles through a terminal lying in their general direction of travel (OR 35(4):543-555). Venue from secondary page.
finder_relevance_note: Analytical trade-off for consolidating many origins through a hub versus direct service, the essential economics of orbital hubs.

id: title:on the location of hub facilities
title: On the Location of Hub Facilities
finder_method_summary: Short technical note (TS 22(2):155-157) on O'Kelly's interacting hub facilities model, discussing the allocation of demand points to hubs and the solution of the continuous hub location problem. Title corroborated by TRID; venue/pages by IDEAS (https://ideas.repec.org/a/inm/ortrsc/v22y1988i2p155-157.html).
finder_relevance_note: Early clarification of allocation logic in hub systems; mainly of historical value for framing the spoke-to-hub assignment subproblem in a spaceport feeder network.

id: title:freight consolidation and routing with transportation economies of scale
title: Freight consolidation and routing with transportation economies of scale
finder_method_summary: Analyses three routing schemes via consolidation terminals in an idealised many-to-many network where consolidation exploits transportation economies of scale; continuous approximation of costs versus number/location of terminals (TR-B 24(5):345-361).
finder_relevance_note: Analytical sizing of how many hubs a many-to-many feeder system should have given scale economies.

title: Solving a Freight Transport Problem Using Facility Location Techniques
finder_method_summary: Freight routing through consolidation terminals with concave (economies-of-scale) link costs reformulated as an uncapacitated facility location problem and solved with facility-location heuristics/dual ascent (OR 38(1):99-109). From title and listing only.
finder_relevance_note: Shows the hub/consolidation routing problem can be cast as facility location, a modelling trick reusable for feeder networks.

id: title:continuous and discrete demand hub location problems
title: Continuous and discrete demand hub location problems
finder_method_summary: Analytical (continuous approximation) hub location models with rectilinear distances comparing transport cost of hub networks for continuously distributed versus discrete demand; derives expressions relating number of hubs, discount and cost, and compares with discrete formulations.
finder_relevance_note: Gives closed-form style sizing of how many hubs a dispersed demand field warrants as a function of the inter-hub discount, useful for order-of-magnitude design of orbital hub count before detailed optimization.

title: Hub Location and the p-Hub Median Problem
finder_method_summary: Integer (linear) programming formulations of the uncapacitated multiple- and single-allocation p-hub median problems with inter-hub discount factor, including variants with flow thresholds and fixed hub costs; discusses LP-relaxation quality and proposes heuristics (e.g., allocation rules derived from the multiple-allocation solution) for the single-allocation case.
finder_relevance_note: Baseline static model for choosing p orbital hubs and assigning each spaceport to one hub (single allocation) or several (multiple allocation) with discounted hub-to-hub transfer; the fixed-cost and threshold variants map to hub set-up and minimum-flow-per-launch conditions.

id: title:hub location with flow economies of scale
title: Hub location with flow economies of scale
finder_method_summary: Argues that fixed inter-hub discount factors miscalculate cost and misplace hubs; introduces the FLOWLOC model with flow-dependent (piecewise-linear concave) inter-hub costs so that scale economies depend on realised bundled flow (TR-B 32(8):605-616).
finder_relevance_note: Core reference for making inter-hub transfer cost depend on consolidated flow volume.

title: Designing Distribution Networks: Formulations and Solution Heuristic
finder_method_summary: Distribution network design formulations with transshipment/consolidation facilities and a solution heuristic; returned for a hub-and-spoke network design query. Title only; year inferred from the trsc.1030 DOI series.

title: Optimal location of intermodal freight hubs
finder_method_summary: Hub location model to raise rail share in intermodal freight via hub-and-spoke networks, generalizing hub location with non-linear concave cost functions on segments; solved via a linearization plus two variable-reduction heuristics exploiting polyhedral results; Alpine freight case study.
finder_relevance_note: Concave-cost hub consolidation is the core economics of spaceport feeder consolidation.

id: title:the latest arrival hub location problem for cargo delivery systems with stopovers
title: The latest arrival hub location problem for cargo delivery systems with stopovers
finder_method_summary: Minimax hub location minimising the arrival time of the last item, including transient (unloading/loading/sorting) times from non-simultaneous arrivals at hubs and allowing stopovers on spoke routes; generic MIP strengthened with valid inequalities and lifting; US and Turkey data (TR-B 41(8):906-919).
finder_relevance_note: Latest-arrival objectives with synchronisation waiting at hubs match orbital rendezvous timing and multi-stop feeder legs.

title: Benders Decomposition for Hub Location Problems with Economies of Scale
finder_method_summary: Multiple-allocation hub-and-spoke network with flow-dependent (piecewise) economies of scale on inter-hub arcs; a tighter MIP formulation and a specialised Benders decomposition solve large instances in reasonable time (TS 43(1):86-97).
finder_relevance_note: Flow-dependent discounts on hub-to-hub legs correspond to consolidated inter-orbit transfers; Benders is the standard exact route for large spoke sets.

id: title:the design of single allocation incomplete hub networks
title: The design of single allocation incomplete hub networks
finder_method_summary: Uniform modelling of single-allocation hub problems when the inter-hub network need not be complete: incomplete p-hub median, hub location with fixed costs, hub covering and p-hub center variants with efficient formulations; CAB and Turkish instances (TR-B 43(10):936-951).
finder_relevance_note: Only a subset of inter-hub (inter-orbit) links can be afforded; incomplete hub network design captures this.

id: title:the hierarchical hub median problem with single assignment
title: The hierarchical hub median problem with single assignment
finder_method_summary: Three-level hub network: complete network among central hubs, star networks from hubs to central hubs and from demand centres to hubs; MIP models deciding locations of a given number of hubs and central hubs and the connections to minimise routing cost; CAB and Turkey data (TR-B 43(6):643-658). Venue from repository page and summary.
finder_relevance_note: Multi-level hub hierarchy is a natural template for regional collection points feeding a small set of launch sites.

title: Single-assignment hub location problems with multiple capacity levels
finder_method_summary: Extends the capacitated single-allocation hub location problem by making hub size a decision chosen from a discrete set of capacity levels. Several MIP formulations are compared via LP-relaxation bounds, strengthened with valid inequalities, and preprocessing tests reduce model size.
finder_relevance_note: Hub sizing with discrete capacity options maps directly to choosing spaceport/consolidation-node capacities in a feeder network.

title: Benders Decomposition for Large-Scale Uncapacitated Hub Location
finder_method_summary: Uncapacitated multiple-allocation hub location with fixed hub set-up costs on a complete hub network, formulated as a path-based MIP and decomposed by Benders: the subproblem separates by origin-destination pair, Pareto-optimal cuts, a multi-cut scheme, elimination tests and a warm-start heuristic are added. Solved instances with up to 500 nodes to optimality, far beyond prior exact methods.
finder_relevance_note: Choosing a small set of orbital hubs among many candidate orbits or stations to serve many spaceport origins is a large-scale hub location instance; this Benders scheme is the exact-method backbone for that choice (

id: title:intermodal hub and spoke network design incorporating multiple stakeholders and multi type
title: Intermodal hub-and-spoke network design: Incorporating multiple stakeholders and multi-type containers
finder_method_summary: Mathematical program with equilibrium constraints for intermodal hub-and-spoke design: network designer at the upper level, parametric variational inequality capturing user-equilibrium route choice of intermodal operators and multi-type containers at the lower level; heuristic solution (TR-B 45(4):724-742).
finder_relevance_note: Multi-stakeholder hub design (infrastructure owner vs launch operators choosing routes) with heterogeneous payload types.

title: Exact Solution of Large-Scale Hub Location Problems with Multiple Capacity Levels
finder_method_summary: Capacitated hub location where each hub is installed at one of several discrete capacity levels; exact algorithm based on Lagrangean relaxation bounds and branch-and-bound/reduction tests, solving large instances (TS 46(4):439-459). From title/index only.
finder_relevance_note: Discrete capacity levels map to sizing orbital hubs (docking ports, propellant/payload storage modules).

title: Hub location under uncertainty
finder_method_summary: Introduces uncertainty in hub set-up costs and in demand into single- and multiple-allocation hub location; scenario-based two-stage stochastic MIPs (location first, allocation/routing by scenario) and a robust (minimax) variant; computational study shows that designs from expected-value deterministic models can differ substantially from stochastic solutions. IAOR corroborates title; volume 46(4):529-543 from recollection.
finder_relevance_note: Template for orbital hub siting when hub set-up cost (construction/launch cost to orbit) and spaceport demand are both uncertain; establishes the value of scenario-based over expected-value design.

id: title:release time scheduling and hub location for next day delivery
title: Release Time Scheduling and Hub Location for Next-Day Delivery
finder_method_summary: Selects p hubs, single-allocates demand centres and decides truck release (departure) times so that the cargo guaranteed to arrive next day at every destination meets a threshold while routing cost is minimised; MIP models with valid inequalities and computational study on Turkish data. Venue stated on secondary pages only.
finder_relevance_note: Joint hub choice and departure-time scheduling under a delivery deadline is a direct analog of launch-window timing into orbital hubs.

title: Twenty-Five Years of Hub Location Research
finder_method_summary: Retrospective survey (TS 46(2):153-169) tracing hub location from O'Kelly's 1986-87 interacting-hub models through p-hub median/center/covering, single vs. multiple allocation, hub arc location and flow-dependent (economies-of-scale) discounts, and linking hub location to classical location analysis and network design. Identifies modelling gaps (constant inter-hub discount, ignoring capacity/congestion, time) and research directions.
finder_relevance_note: Provides the taxonomy of hub models (median/center/covering, allocation rules, arc vs node hubs, discount structure) from which a spaceport-spoke / orbital-hub design can be classified, and warns that constant inter-hub discounts misrepresent vehicle cost structures such as launch economics.

title: Hub Location as the Minimization of a Supermodular Set Function
finder_method_summary: Shows that a general class of hub location problems (uncapacitated hub location, p-hub median, hub arc location, etc.) is the minimisation of a supermodular set function over hub sets; derives compact formulations and supermodular inequalities enabling branch-and-cut (OR 62(3):557-570).
finder_relevance_note: Unifying structure that yields strong cuts for any hub-set selection, including orbital-hub choice.

title: The Hub Line Location Problem
authors: Martins de Sá, Contreras, Cordeau, de Camargo, de Miranda
finder_method_summary: Locates hubs connected by a path (line) rather than a complete inter-hub graph, minimising weighted travel time including access/exit times; exact Benders decomposition of a strong path-based formulation with multicuts, a fast subproblem algorithm, stronger optimality cuts and Benders branch-and-cut (TS 49(3):500-518). Result page lists the first three authors; remaining two from the paper's author list.
finder_relevance_note: Incomplete inter-hub topologies (a chain of orbital nodes, e.g. LEO depot to higher-energy hub) rather than full interconnection.

title: The reliable hub-and-spoke design problem: Models and algorithms
finder_method_summary: Hub-and-spoke design in which hubs may be disrupted: each O-D pair is given a primary hub route and backup hubs/routes used upon failure; nonlinear integer programs are linearized and solved by Lagrangian relaxation with branch-and-bound, showing reliable designs cost little extra in normal operation.
finder_relevance_note: Provides the backup-hub and re-routing logic needed when an orbital hub is unavailable (outage, phasing window missed), a key robustness feature for a spaceport feeder network.

id: title:robust intermodal hub location under polyhedral demand uncertainty
title: Robust intermodal hub location under polyhedral demand uncertainty
finder_method_summary: Robust uncapacitated multiple-allocation p-hub median under polyhedral demand uncertainty (hose model with node-flow upper limits, hybrid model adding pairwise bounds); minmax linear MIP formulations and two Benders-decomposition exact algorithms for large instances (TR-B 86:66-85).
finder_relevance_note: Hose-type uncertainty (known per-spaceport totals, unknown O-D split) is realistic for payload demand forecasts.

id: title:the design of capacitated intermodal hub networks with different vehicle types
title: The design of capacitated intermodal hub networks with different vehicle types
finder_method_summary: Determines hub locations and capacities, which transport modes each hub serves, allocation of non-hub nodes and the number of vehicles of each type on hub-network arcs; MIP with a variable-neighbourhood-search heuristic for large instances (TR-B 86:51-65).
finder_relevance_note: Explicit vehicle-count decisions per arc are the launch-vehicle fleet sizing embedded in feeder hub design.

title: Robust uncapacitated hub location
finder_method_summary: Robust counterparts of uncapacitated multiple-allocation hub location under interval demand uncertainty, interval transportation-cost uncertainty, and both, using Bertsimas-Sim budgeted uncertainty; compact MIP reformulations solved by a Benders-based branch-and-cut, with the price of robustness quantified on CAB/AP instances.
finder_relevance_note: Budgeted robustness lets a feeder-network designer protect the orbital-hub choice against bounded deviations in payload demand and launch cost without full scenario trees.

title: Solving Single Allocation Hub Location Problems on Euclidean Data
finder_method_summary: Single-allocation hub location on Euclidean instances using a compact formulation that exploits the geometric distance structure, solved by branch-and-cut; solves standard AP instances up to 200 nodes to optimality that earlier exact methods could not.
finder_relevance_note: Scalable exact solution of single-allocation designs when feeder costs follow a metric (e.g., distance- or delta-v-like structure), useful for networks with many candidate spaceports.

id: title:benders decomposition for the design of a hub and shuttle public transit system
title: Benders Decomposition for the Design of a Hub and Shuttle Public Transit System
finder_method_summary: Design of a hub-and-shuttle transit system (bus hubs with feeder shuttles) via Benders decomposition. Search summary gives vol 53(1):77-88, 2019, which matches Transportation Science, but names the venue inconsistently; publisher page not seen.
finder_relevance_note: Hub plus feeder-shuttle structure is the transit analog of spaceport spokes feeding orbital hubs.

title: Heuristic Solutions for a Class of Stochastic Uncapacitated p-Hub Median Problems
finder_method_summary: r-allocation p-hub median extended with fixed allocation costs, non-stop (direct) services between terminals and stochastic traffic and transport costs with finite support; heuristic (GRASP/path-relinking style) producing high-quality feasible solutions (TS 53(4):1126-1149).
finder_relevance_note: Combines allocation flexibility, direct shipments and demand uncertainty, all features of a spaceport feeder design with uncertain payload demand.

title: Benders Decomposition for the Profit Maximizing Capacitated Hub Location Problem with Multiple Demand Classes
finder_method_summary: Profit-maximising capacitated hub location with several demand classes having different revenues/service requirements, allowing demand to be left unserved; exact Benders decomposition with enhancements for large instances.
finder_relevance_note: Payload classes (crew, priority cargo, bulk) with different willingness-to-pay and the option to drop unprofitable spaceports.

title: Distributionally Robust Hub Location
finder_method_summary: Hub location under demand ambiguity described by a moment-based ambiguity set; the distributionally robust model is reformulated via duality into a tractable mixed-integer program and solved with a decomposition / cutting-plane scheme, showing DRO designs hedge mis-specified demand at modest cost.
finder_relevance_note: Launch demand forecasts for new orbital services are poorly characterised distributions, so a moment-based DRO hub model is a direct fit for depot location under deep demand uncertainty.

id: title:hub location routing and route dimensioning strategic and tactical intermodal transportati
title: Hub Location, Routing, and Route Dimensioning: Strategic and Tactical Intermodal Transportation Hub Network Design
finder_method_summary: Integrated strategic/tactical model that locates hubs, allocates demand nodes, routes commodities over an intermodal hub network and dimensions routes (number and type of vehicles per hub arc) subject to service-time limits; mixed-integer formulation with an exact decomposition-based solution approach, tested on intermodal instances. Index page corroborates TS 55(6):1351-1369 and the search summary cites 'strategic and tactical intermodal transportation hub network design' in TS; author list from recollection.
finder_relevance_note: Closest hub-location analog to the spaceport problem: it jointly chooses hubs, vehicle types and the number of vehicles on each feeder/inter-hub leg under delivery-time limits, i.e., launch-vehicle class and launch count per route.

title: Robust Stochastic Models for Profit-Maximizing Hub Location Problems
finder_method_summary: Profit-maximizing capacitated hub location with uncertain demand and revenues, modelled as two-stage stochastic programs and robust-stochastic variants that hedge over scenario distributions; solved with Benders decomposition combined with sample average approximation, comparing risk-neutral and risk-averse hub designs.
finder_relevance_note: Capacitated orbital hubs serving uncertain payload demand with class-dependent revenues can be sized and located with the same Benders-SAA machinery, letting the model drop unprofitable spaceports.

title: Single Allocation Hub Location with Heterogeneous Economies of Scale
finder_method_summary: Single-allocation hub location where inter-hub discount factors depend on the flow (heterogeneous, piecewise economies of scale); mixed-integer nonlinear formulation with linearisation/convexification and an exact decomposition algorithm.
finder_relevance_note: Vehicle-size-dependent cost per kg on consolidated inter-orbit legs is a heterogeneous economies-of-scale structure.

id: title:the stratified p hub center and p hub maximal covering problems
title: The stratified p-hub center and p-hub maximal covering problems
finder_method_summary: Multiple-allocation p-hub center and p-hub maximal covering where each O-D pair's traffic is split into strata with distinct service-level (time) requirements; MILP models and efficient Benders decomposition algorithms for large instances (TR-B 157:120-148).
finder_relevance_note: Service-level strata per O-D pair correspond to payload classes with different delivery-time guarantees via orbital hubs.

title: Toward a Reference Experimental Benchmark for Solving Hub Location Problems
finder_method_summary: Systematic computational benchmark of exact and heuristic methods across standard hub location variants and instance sets, proposing a reference experimental protocol.
finder_relevance_note: Guides choice of solution method and instance scale for a feeder-network hub model.

title: Demand-Driven Hub Network Design Under Uncertainty for Less-Than-Truckload Carriers
finder_relevance_note: Most recent in-scope treatment of consolidation hub network design under demand uncertainty, the closest commercial analogue to spaceport-to-hub payload consolidation; details need a second search round.

title: Network Design and Transportation Planning: Models and Algorithms
finder_method_summary: Survey/unifying framework for discrete-choice network design as integer programs over fixed-charge multicommodity flow networks; reviews Benders, Lagrangian and dual-ascent algorithms and computational experience; foundation of the fixed-charge capacitated multicommodity network design lineage.
finder_relevance_note: Root model class for choosing which spaceport-hub launch services to open (fixed charge) and routing payload flows over them.

title: A Local Improvement Heuristic for the Design of Less-than-Truckload Motor Carrier Networks
finder_method_summary: Early service network design for LTL consolidation networks: local-improvement (add/drop of direct services) heuristic over a load-planning network with consolidation at break-bulk terminals.
finder_relevance_note: Classic hub-and-spoke consolidation design heuristic transferable to spoke-to-hub feeder service selection.

id: title:multicommodity multimode freight transportation a general modeling and algorithmic framewo
title: Multicommodity, multimode freight transportation: A general modeling and algorithmic framework for the service network design problem
finder_method_summary: Seminal frequency-based SND: nonlinear mixed-integer model choosing service frequencies and commodity itineraries (paths) with congestion/delay costs at terminals; heuristic decomposition alternating itinerary column generation with descent on service frequencies. RePEc URL (TRB 20(3), 225-242) surfaced for the Crainic SND query.
finder_relevance_note: The frequency-and-itinerary view (how often to serve each spaceport-hub corridor, which payload paths to use, congestion at hubs) is the tactical layer of feeder design before detailed time-expanded scheduling.

id: title:a dual ascent procedure for large scale uncapacitated network design
title: A Dual-Ascent Procedure for Large-Scale Uncapacitated Network Design
finder_method_summary: Dual-ascent (Lagrangian/dual) algorithm producing near-optimal bounds for large uncapacitated fixed-charge network design.
finder_relevance_note: Classic bounding technique for fixed-charge network design.

id: title:subgradient methods for the service network design problem
title: Subgradient Methods for the Service Network Design Problem
finder_method_summary: Service network design over a time-space network for LTL carriers; subgradient-based (dual) methods combined with add/drop of services, using primal-dual information from the multicommodity flow subproblem.
finder_relevance_note: Early scheduled-SND formulation on a time-space network with vehicle balance, directly analogous to scheduling launch services.

title: Solving the uncapacitated network design problem by a Lagrangean heuristic and branch-and-bound
finder_method_summary: Exact branch-and-bound for uncapacitated fixed-charge network design using Lagrangian heuristic bounds. DOI in result text only.
finder_relevance_note: Exact baseline for fixed-charge network design.

title: A Lagrangian Heuristic Based Branch-and-Bound Approach for the Capacitated Network Design Problem
finder_method_summary: Exact branch-and-bound for fixed-charge capacitated multicommodity network design with Lagrangian relaxation bounds and a Lagrangian heuristic for primal solutions.
finder_relevance_note: Exact method for the capacitated fixed-charge core of a feeder network design.

title: Dynamic Routing for Priority Shipments in LTL Service Networks
finder_method_summary: Dynamic routing of priority shipments through an LTL service network given the load plan. From title only.
finder_relevance_note: Operational routing of time-critical payload over a fixed feeder service network.

title: Design of Capacitated Multicommodity Networks with Multiple Facilities
finder_method_summary: Capacitated multicommodity network loading in which several facility types with different costs and capacities can be installed on each edge (motivated by private telecom networks using Fractional-T1 services); integer-programming formulation solved with strengthened (partition/cut-set type) inequalities and branch-and-bound.
finder_relevance_note: Choosing among launch-vehicle classes with different payload capacities and costs on each spaceport-to-orbit corridor is a multi-facility capacitated network loading problem; the cutting-plane approach transfers directly.

title: Cycle-Based Neighbourhoods for Fixed-Charge Capacitated Multicommodity Network Design
finder_method_summary: Arc-based MIP for the fixed-charge capacitated multicommodity network design (CMND) problem: open arcs at fixed cost and route commodity flows at linear cost subject to arc capacity. Proposes cycle-based neighbourhoods for tabu search in which a move redirects flow around a cycle (opening/closing arcs) and candidate cycles are identified by shortest-path-like network procedures; outperforms earlier arc/path-based tabu heuristics on benchmark CMND instances.
finder_relevance_note: Selecting which spaceport-to-hub launch services to open at fixed cost while routing payload flows under per-launch capacity is a CMND; cycle-based moves give a scalable heuristic for large feeder instances where exact MIP fails.

title: Discretization and Validation of the Continuum Approximation Scheme for Terminal System Design
finder_method_summary: Algorithm that translates continuum-approximation (CA) location recipes into discrete terminal designs and validates CA accuracy for terminal systems. DOI stated in result text, publisher URL not seen.
finder_relevance_note: Bridges analytical hub-count/frequency estimates and a discrete spaceport-hub design.

title: Models and Tabu Search Metaheuristics for Service Network Design with Asset-Balance Requirements
finder_method_summary: Design-balanced capacitated multicommodity network design (DBCMND) with constraints balancing assets at terminals on a time-space network; arc- and cycle-based formulations; tabu search on the arc formulation tested on standard instances.
finder_relevance_note: Design-balance constraints model reusable launch vehicles returning to spaceports between missions.

title: Cutting-Plane Matheuristic for Service Network Design with Design-Balanced Requirements
finder_method_summary: Design-balanced capacitated multicommodity network design solved by a cutting-plane procedure (tight lower bounds, learning which variables are promising) feeding a variable-fixing MIP phase.
finder_relevance_note: Exact-bound-guided heuristic for balanced-asset feeder designs.

title: Enabling Urban Logistics Services at La Poste through Multi-Echelon Location-Routing
finder_method_summary: Multi-echelon location-routing model with continuous-approximation routing cost estimates for urban logistics facility design.
finder_relevance_note: Multi-echelon facility design with approximated routing cost; by-catch for the location-routing facet.

id: title:commodity representations and cut set based inequalities for multicommodity capacitated fi
title: Commodity Representations and Cut-Set-Based Inequalities for Multicommodity Capacitated Fixed-Charge Network Design
finder_method_summary: Cutting-plane algorithm for MCFND using strong, cover, minimum cardinality, flow cover and flow pack inequalities expressed on network cut sets; compares aggregated vs disaggregated commodity representations.
finder_relevance_note: Strengthened formulations for the capacitated fixed-charge core of the feeder design.

title: Reformulations by Discretization for Piecewise Linear Integer Multicommodity Network Flow Problems
finder_method_summary: Discretization-based reformulations (unit-capacity/staircase cost) for multicommodity network flow with piecewise linear integer costs, generalizing fixed-charge network design; stronger relaxations.
finder_relevance_note: Models stepwise launch cost as a function of number of vehicles dispatched on a lane.

title: Robust Service Network Design Under Demand Uncertainty

finder_method_summary: Extends flow-interception location to allow customers to deviate from preplanned paths at a cost; models market size versus inconvenience trade-off and gives formulations and approximation algorithms (OR 43(4):623-632).
finder_relevance_note: Deviation-tolerant interception models underlie later range-limited refuelling and charging-hub location, the hub-with-capacity analog for feeder networks.

title: A Branch-and-Cut Algorithm for the Alternative Fuel Refueling Station Location Problem with Routing
finder_method_summary: Locates refuelling stations for range-limited vehicles while allowing drivers to deviate from shortest paths (routing); branch-and-cut on a natural formulation with path/range feasibility cuts. From URL/title only; DOI in the 2018 series (likely published 2019).
finder_relevance_note: Locating replenishment nodes so that range-limited vehicles can complete paths is the terrestrial analog of placing staging/refuelling hubs along spoke-to-orbit chains.
