title: Optimization Approaches for the Traveling Salesman Problem with Drone
finder_method_summary: Introduces the TSP with Drone (TSP-D): a truck and a drone jointly serve customers, the drone launching from and returning to the truck under a flight-range limit. MIP formulation plus route-first, cluster-second heuristics based on local search and dynamic programming; shows substantial savings over truck-only delivery.
finder_relevance_note: Fast range-limited vehicle synchronized with a slower high-capacity carrier is the structural analog of launch vehicles with limited windows feeding from ground spokes.

title: Drone routing with energy function: Formulation and exact algorithm
finder_method_summary: Multi-trip drone routing from a depot where energy consumption is a nonlinear function of payload and distance; 2-index and 3-index formulations with logic-based cuts, solved by branch-and-cut; shows the value of modelling the energy function explicitly (TR-B 139:364-387).
finder_relevance_note: Payload-dependent energy/range of a vehicle returning to a hub is a direct analog of payload-dependent launch-vehicle capacity and delta-v budgets.

title: Exact and Heuristic Algorithms for the Carrier–Vehicle Traveling Salesman Problem
finder_method_summary: Carrier-vehicle TSP: a slow, long-range carrier (e.g., ship) transports a fast, range-limited vehicle (e.g., helicopter) that visits targets and returns to the carrier; exact and heuristic algorithms. From URL/title only; DOI in the 2020 series (likely published 2021).
finder_relevance_note: Mothership-and-satellite routing is the closest routing analog to a reusable launcher staging from a carrier hub with limited sortie range.
year_note: year taken from DOI (submission year); publication may be one year later

title: Same-Day Delivery with Drone Resupply
finder_method_summary: Introduces the vehicle routing problem with drone resupply: delivery trucks are resupplied in the field by drones from the depot whenever stationary, so trucks need not return. Dynamic same-day setting; optimization-based heuristics evaluated in simulation show reductions in delivery time and fleet size (TS 54(1):229-249).
finder_relevance_note: Hub-to-vehicle resupply with time-limited rendezvous is an analog of feeding payload to a launch asset within a time window rather than returning to the hub.

title: Charging Station Location and Sizing for Electric Vehicles Under Congestion
finder_method_summary: Joint location and sizing of charging stations with queueing/congestion at stations (capacitated facilities with waiting), formulated and solved as a capacitated location model with congestion terms. From URL/title only; DOI in the 2021 series (likely published 2022-2023).
finder_relevance_note: Hub-with-capacity-and-congestion location is the generic form of both vertiport charging-pad sizing and orbital/ground hub docking capacity.
year_note: year taken from DOI (submission year); publication may be one year later

title: Coordinated Logistics with a Truck and Multiple Sidekicks
finder_method_summary: Truck coordinated with multiple drones (sidekicks); extends the single-drone coordinated-logistics analysis to several range-limited satellite vehicles. From URL/title only; DOI in the 2021 series (likely published 2022).
finder_relevance_note: One carrier serving many range-limited satellites approximates one orbital hub served by several limited-capacity launch vehicles.
year_note: year taken from DOI (submission year); publication may be one year later

title: Exact Methods for the Traveling Salesman Problem with Drone
finder_method_summary: Exact solution of TSP-D variants (truck with large capacity and low urban speed; drone fast, off-network, range- and payload-limited). Compact MIP and a branch-and-price approach with ng-route-type relaxations and dynamic programming pricing; solves larger instances than earlier exact methods (TS 55(2):315-335).
finder_relevance_note: Exact decomposition for synchronized carrier/satellite-vehicle schedules transfers to synchronized spoke-to-launcher feeding with capacity and range limits.

title: Minimizing energy and cost in range-limited drone deliveries with speed optimization
finder_method_summary: Energy Minimizing and Range Constrained Drone Delivery Problem: trucks act as launch bases for drones; nonlinear model minimizing operating plus energy cost with drone speed as a decision, service-time bounds and range limits; solved via second-order cone reformulation and heuristics. Published in TR-C 125 (the facet brief listed TR-B).
finder_relevance_note: Jointly choosing launch bases and vehicle speed/energy under range limits parallels choosing spaceport staging and trajectory energy budgets.

title: Cooperative Learning for Smart Charging of Shared Autonomous Vehicle Fleets
finder_method_summary: Operational charging control for shared autonomous (electric) vehicle fleets using cooperative/multi-agent learning to decide when and where vehicles charge given station capacity. From URL/title only; DOI in the 2022 series.
finder_relevance_note: Fleet-level charging/turnaround coordination at capacitated stations is the operational counterpart of RAM aircraft charging slots (A) and reusable-vehicle turnaround scheduling (B).
year_note: year taken from DOI (submission year); publication may be one year later

title: Robust Charging Network Planning for Metropolitan Taxi Fleets
finder_method_summary: Plans a charging-station network (locations and charger counts) for an electric taxi fleet under uncertain demand using robust optimization. From URL/title only; DOI in the 2022 series (likely published 2023-2024).
finder_relevance_note: Robust sizing of capacitated energy-replenishment hubs for a fleet transfers to vertiport/airport charging capacity (A) and to turnaround capacity at spaceport hubs under demand uncertainty (B).
year_note: year taken from DOI (submission year); publication may be one year later

title: The Traveling Salesman Problem with Drones: The Benefits of Retraversing the Arcs
finder_method_summary: TSP with drones in which the truck may retraverse arcs; quantifies the benefit of allowing repeated arc use for truck-drone synchronization. From URL/title only; DOI in the 2022 series (likely TS 57, 2023; an IDEAS handle ortrsc/v57y2023i5p1340-1358 appeared in the same result set).
finder_relevance_note: Shows how relaxing path structure of the carrier improves synchronized satellite operations, relevant to flexible routing of feeder legs to launch sites.
year_note: year taken from DOI (submission year); publication may be one year later

title: The Orienteering Problem with Drones
finder_method_summary: Orienteering (profit-collecting, time-limited) variant with a truck and drones; selects which customers to serve within a time budget subject to drone range and synchronization. From URL/title only; DOI in the 2023 series (likely published 2024).
finder_relevance_note: Selective service under a hard time budget with range-limited satellites maps to choosing which spokes a launch window can serve.
year_note: year taken from DOI (submission year); publication may be one year later

title: Mathematical formulations for the multi-period alternative fuel refueling station location problem with routing under decision-dependent flow dynamics
finder_method_summary: Multi-period location of alternative-fuel refuelling stations where range-limited vehicles may deviate from shortest paths and the flow (adoption) in each period depends on the stations already opened (decision-dependent dynamics).
finder_relevance_note: Phased infrastructure roll-out where demand responds to opened facilities parallels staged spaceport/hub capacity expansion under adoption-dependent demand.

title: Optimizing an On-Demand Delivery Mode Based on Trucks and Drones
finder_method_summary: A fleet of trucks, each carrying several drones, circulates on closed-loop routes; drones pick up and deliver parcels and parcels can transship between routes. MIP for the multi-route network with transshipment; studies number of drones, speed, endurance, penalty cost and spatial order distribution (TS 59(5):1008-1031).
finder_relevance_note: Cyclic trunk routes with drone spokes and inter-route transshipment mirror periodic launch cycles fed by spokes with transfer at hubs.

id: title:the multiregion dynamic capacity expansion problem part i
title: The Multiregion Dynamic Capacity Expansion Problem, Part I
finder_method_summary: Multi-region, multi-period capacity expansion with inter-regional transportation: when and where to add capacity to satisfy growing regional demands; heuristic based on single-region DP subproblems.
finder_relevance_note: Where/when to add launch or hub capacity across regions with transshipment between them.

id: title:the multiregion dynamic capacity expansion problem part ii
title: The Multiregion Dynamic Capacity Expansion Problem, Part II

finder_relevance_note: Same transfer as Part I.

title: Operations Research and Capacity Expansion Problems: A Survey
finder_method_summary: Unifying survey of capacity expansion models: single/multi-facility, deterministic and stochastic demand growth, timing and sizing of expansions, economies of scale; DP, network and heuristic algorithms and applications.
finder_relevance_note: Foundational taxonomy for expanding spaceport/hub capacity over time under demand growth.

title: Fleet Sizing under Production Cycles and Uncertain Travel Times
finder_method_summary: Analytical/stochastic model of the number of reusable containers (vehicles) needed to sustain a cyclic production-shipment loop when travel/turnaround times are uncertain; fleet size follows from cycle time distribution and service-level targets.
finder_relevance_note: Direct analog for sizing a reusable launch-vehicle fleet whose turnaround (refurbishment + return) time is uncertain and whose service runs on a repeating cycle.

title: Survey Paper—A Review of Empty Flows and Fleet Management Models in Freight Transportation
finder_method_summary: Taxonomy and literature review of empty-vehicle flow and fleet management models (strategic fleet sizing, tactical allocation, operational dispatching; deterministic vs stochastic; network-flow and DP formulations).
finder_relevance_note: Organizing framework for the empty-return (vehicle repositioning) layer of a spaceport feeder network with reusable vehicles.

title: A Model for Fleet Sizing and Vehicle Allocation
finder_method_summary: Joint optimization of fleet size and dynamic allocation of loaded/empty vehicles over a time-space network with uncertain demand; expected-value nonlinear network model in which fleet size and utilization interact, solved by an iterative network-optimization procedure. Shows fleet sizing and empty allocation must be decided together.
finder_relevance_note: Template for jointly choosing the launch-vehicle fleet size and the repositioning of empty vehicles among spaceports under uncertain payload demand.

title: Capacity Expansion Under Stochastic Demands
finder_method_summary: Shows that capacity expansion under certain stochastic demand processes can be transformed into an equivalent deterministic problem by rescaling time/discount rate, enabling deterministic expansion algorithms.
finder_relevance_note: Simplifies hub/launch-capacity expansion timing under uncertain demand growth.

title: Dynamic and Stochastic Models for the Allocation of Empty Containers
finder_method_summary: Dynamic deterministic and stochastic network models for allocating empty containers among depots/ports over a multi-period horizon, including substitution between container types and uncertain supplies/demands; time-space multicommodity flow formulations. Seen only as a citation in a result (no publisher URL).
finder_relevance_note: Foundational time-expanded asset-balancing formulation; the spaceport analogue is repositioning reusable vehicles and containers among spokes.

id: title:a survey of optimization models for train routing and scheduling
title: A Survey of Optimization Models for Train Routing and Scheduling
finder_method_summary: Survey of optimization models for rail routing and scheduling including locomotive and rolling-stock assignment and rotation. Seen only in a reference list (TS 32:380-404).
finder_relevance_note: Background for cyclic asset-rotation models applicable to reusable vehicle turnaround.

title: A Tactical Decision Support System for Empty Railcar Management
finder_method_summary: Multicommodity network flow model on a time-space network for tactical distribution of empty railcars with train-capacity constraints and substitution between car types; solved by Lagrangian-relaxation-based heuristics for a national railway.
finder_relevance_note: Capacitated time-space repositioning of reusable assets with substitutable types resembles returning launch vehicles/capsules through capacitated scheduled links.

title: A Two-Stage Stochastic Network Model and Solution Methods for the Dynamic Empty Container Allocation Problem
finder_method_summary: Two-stage stochastic network model on a time-space network: stage-one supplies, demands and ship capacities deterministic, stage-two random; exploits network structure to apply stochastic quasi-gradient and stochastic hybrid approximation procedures.
finder_relevance_note: Stochastic time-expanded repositioning of reusable assets with capacitated, scheduled links (ships ~ launch slots) maps directly onto the spaceport feeder problem.

id: title:dynamic control of logistics queueing networks for large scale fleet management
title: Dynamic Control of Logistics Queueing Networks for Large-Scale Fleet Management
finder_method_summary: Formulates dynamic fleet management as an optimal control problem over a Logistics Queueing Network, replacing one large time-space LP by a sequence of small local problems with value-based gradients; achieves solutions within a few percent of global optimum with much more modeling flexibility.
finder_relevance_note: Scalable decomposition for dispatching reusable vehicles among many spokes when demand arrives dynamically.

id: title:a multiplier adjustment method for dynamic resource allocation problems
title: A Multiplier Adjustment Method for Dynamic Resource Allocation Problems
finder_method_summary: Multiplier (dual) adjustment method for dynamic resource allocation on time-space networks, building on the LQN framework to approximate the value of resources in future periods. Title seen on a Princeton page; volume/pages matched via IDEAS (TS 34(2):150-164).
finder_relevance_note: Dual-price based coordination of vehicle allocation across periods/locations is reusable for launch-vehicle allocation.

title: An Adaptive Dynamic Programming Algorithm for Dynamic Fleet Management, I: Single Period Travel Times
finder_method_summary: Approximate dynamic programming for stochastic dynamic fleet management: piecewise-linear concave, separable value-function approximations of future resource value are learned adaptively from sample gradients and naturally yield integer solutions to the per-period network subproblems.
finder_relevance_note: ADP with concave value functions handles stochastic payload demand and vehicle repositioning decisions over many periods in the feeder network.

title: An Adaptive Dynamic Programming Algorithm for Dynamic Fleet Management, II: Multiperiod Travel Times
finder_method_summary: Extends Part I to multiperiod travel times, where the basic algorithm performed poorly; a modified algorithm that accounts for vehicles in transit restores near-Part-I performance.
finder_relevance_note: Launch-and-return trips span multiple periods (orbital phasing, refurbishment), exactly the in-transit resource issue solved here.

title: An Approximation Scheme for Stochastic Integer Programs Arising in Capacity Expansion
finder_method_summary: Multi-stage stochastic integer program for capacity expansion over a scenario tree; LP-relaxation-based heuristic shown to be asymptotically optimal as the number of periods grows.
finder_relevance_note: Multi-stage expansion of launch/hub capacity under demand scenarios.

title: An Integrated Model and Solution Approach for Fleet Sizing with Heterogeneous Assets
finder_method_summary: LP on a time-space network that integrates operational decisions (demand allocation, empty repositioning) with tactical asset procurement/sale decisions for assets of different ages with age-dependent costs, yielding optimal fleet size and mix; two-phase solution approach for large instances (truck rental).
finder_relevance_note: Shows how fleet size/mix and vehicle acquisition-retirement (finite reuse life of launch vehicles) can be embedded in a time-expanded repositioning model.

title: Solving Real-Life Locomotive-Scheduling Problems
finder_method_summary: Weekly locomotive assignment as a multicommodity flow on a space-time network with consist constraints; solved by problem decomposition, integer programming and very large-scale neighborhood search within 30 minutes for U.S. railroads.
finder_relevance_note: Assigning reusable propulsion assets to scheduled services with consistency constraints, a close analog of launch-vehicle-to-launch assignment.

title: A model for the fleet sizing of demand responsive transportation services with time windows
finder_method_summary: Probabilistic model to determine the number of vehicles needed for a demand-responsive service with prescribed quality (waiting time and maximum detour), requiring only the spatial demand distribution and pickup/delivery time windows; positioned as a lighter alternative to simulation when detailed demand data are lacking.
finder_relevance_note: Analytical fleet-sizing under time-window quality targets applies to RAM on-demand fleets and feeder vehicle counts.

title: Incorporating Pricing Decisions into the Stochastic Dynamic Fleet Management Problem
finder_method_summary: Joint pricing and fleet management: ADP value function approximations for the stochastic dynamic fleet problem are combined with price-dependent demand so that prices and vehicle allocations are optimized together.
finder_relevance_note: Suggests coupling launch pricing with fleet repositioning in the feeder network under demand uncertainty.

title: Sensitivity Analysis of a Dynamic Fleet Management Model Using Approximate Dynamic Programming
finder_method_summary: Tractable algorithms to compute the marginal value of an additional vehicle or load in a stochastic dynamic fleet management model solved by ADP, without re-simulation; numerically accurate and cheap.
finder_relevance_note: Gives the marginal value of one more reusable vehicle, i.e., a fleet-sizing signal, directly from the operational model.

title: Scheduling Locomotives and Car Transfers in Freight Transport
finder_method_summary: MIP for simultaneous locomotive scheduling and car-transfer planning in freight rail with cyclic timetable; solved with commercial MIP plus problem-specific cuts/heuristics.

title: The Locomotive Routing Problem
finder_method_summary: Routes individual locomotive units through a train network so that fueling and maintenance constraints are met; network-based IP formulations on a time-space network with decomposition heuristics.

authors: Simao, Day, George, Gifford, Nienow, Powell

title: Dantzig-Wolfe Decomposition for Solving Multistage Stochastic Capacity-Planning Problems
finder_method_summary: Multistage stochastic MIP for capacity expansion with a scenario tree; variable splitting plus Dantzig-Wolfe gives a master problem with far stronger LP relaxation that tends to yield integer solutions; solved 6-stage, 243-scenario electricity-network instance.
finder_relevance_note: Decomposition recipe for multistage expansion of a capacitated network under uncertain demand.

title: The Value of Multistage Stochastic Programming in Capacity Planning Under Uncertainty
finder_method_summary: Analyzes the value of multistage over two-stage stochastic programming for capacity planning, deriving bounds on the gap and conditions under which multistage models matter; semiconductor capacity case.

title: Branch and Price for Service Network Design with Asset Management Constraints
finder_method_summary: Scheduled service network design on a cyclic time-space network with asset-balance constraints that force each vehicle to follow a closed rotation; the model is written with cycle-based (vehicle-rotation) variables and solved by branch-and-price with column generation over asset cycles, which outperforms arc- and path-based formulations.

title: Network-based real option models

title: Service Network Design with Resource Constraints
